textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models with KL-Regularized Reward Maximization for Text-to-Image Generation
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with a KL-regularized objective for fine-tuning pre-trained diffusion models for text-to-image generation, using a stochastic version of the marginal KL divergence that can be estimated from denoising trajectories. Specifically, we will test the following objective function on the LSUN dataset: maximize the expected reward R(s, a) while minimizing the stochastic KL divergence between the fine-tuned diffusion model and a reference distribution, which is computed as an exponential of the reward along the denoising trajectory. The reference distribution will be the pre-trained diffusion model, and the reward will be a per-sample classification loss.
CONTROLS: We will compare this approach to PPO on the same objective without KL regularization, as well as to fine-tuning without any KL regularization.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: This approach should achieve better results than fine-tuning without any KL regularization, but potentially worse than PPO, due to the stochastic approximation of the KL divergence. However, it could show better stability in large-scale training settings, as the KL regularization helps to prevent drifting away from the pre-trained distribution. We expect failures in settings with extremely high-dimensional images, where the stochastic KL approximation may not be reliable.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Step Trajectory KL Regularization for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with a KL regularization term between entire denoising trajectories, which has been shown to be a relaxation of the marginal KL divergence. However, in our experiments, we will use a modified version of this term, where the KL divergence is computed between the fine-tuned and reference distributions at multiple steps along the denoising trajectory, rather than just at the final step. This could potentially mitigate the initial value function bias problem.
CONTROLS: We will compare this approach to the previous KL-regularized objective, as well as to a baseline where KL regularization is entirely ignored.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: This approach may achieve better results than ignoring KL regularization, but potentially worse than the KL-regularized objective, especially in cases where the initial value function bias is significant. However, it could be a more practical solution that requires less computational resources than computing the stochastic KL divergence. We expect failures in settings where the denoising trajectory is very long, as the intermediate steps may not be well-represented in the reference distribution.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flow Model Rejection Sampling for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with rejection sampling as a fine-tuning mechanism for pre-trained flow models. Specifically, we will train a model to reject a certain percentage of samples generated by the pre-trained flow model, and then fine-tune the flow model on the remaining accepted samples. The rejection likelihood can be learned using a separate model, and we can use techniques like importance weighting to compensate for the rejected samples.
CONTROLS: We will compare this approach to the previous KL-regularized objectives and the baseline where KL regularization is ignored, as well as to a variant where the rejection likelihood is learned via a separate fine-tuning step.
COST: 120000
PREDICTION: This approach may achieve good results, especially in cases where the pre-trained flow model is close to the desired distribution, but the learning process may be unstable due to the complex rejection mechanism. We expect failures in settings where the pre-trained flow model generates samples that are drastically different from the target distribution, or where the rejection likelihood is difficult to learn.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leveraging the Generative Structure of Flow Models for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with transforming the KL-regularized objective so that it takes into account the intermediate noisy states of the flow model. Specifically, we will propose a new objective function that combines the expected reward and a penalty term that measures the difference between the noisy states of the fine-tuned and pre-trained flow models. This penalty term can be computed using a dedicated tracing technique to match the latent spaces of the two models.
CONTROLS: We will compare this approach to the previous KL-regularized objectives and the baseline where KL regularization is ignored, as well as to a variant where the tracing technique is replaced by a simple autoencoder.
COST: 240000
PREDICTION: This approach may achieve better results than the previous KL-regularized objectives, especially in cases where the pre-trained flow model's intermediate noisy states are informative about the target distribution. However, the computation of the penalty term may be expensive, and the model may be prone to local optima if the initial space is not well-distributed. We expect failures in settings where the intermediate noisy states are not informative or are poorly conditioned.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct Measurement of the Implicit Bias of Pre-Trained Diffusion Models Using a Self-Supervised Calibration Step
PROPOSAL: We will design a self-supervised calibration step to directly estimate the implicit bias in the pre-trained diffusion model's performance, enabling informed bias mitigation during fine-tuning. This involves augmenting the training objective with a separate auxiliary task that measures how the model's predictions change under perturbations that simulate real-world variability, and then estimating the bias as the difference between the model's performance on the original and perturbed data distributions.
CONTROLS: We will test for different strengths of perturbation and different calibration protocols.
COST: 720000
PREDICTION: This approach may provide a more accurate and understandable measure of the implicit bias of pre-trained diffusion models, but may require large additional computational resources, and the choice of calibration protocol may significantly affect the results. We expect higher inaccuracies in settings where the self-supervised objective and the main task have overlapping features, but the estimation is subsequently scorched out with perturbation measurements as we prove to reasonably generalise this with testing.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Regularization of the Denoising Path to Improve Sample Quality
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with a regularization term that lives in the space of the denoising path, forcing the pre-trained diffusion model to produce samples that are closer to the data distribution. Specifically, we will use a loss function that measures the difference between the noisy states generated during the denoising process and the samples drawn from the target distribution.
CONTROLS: We will compare this approach to the previous proposals, including the KL-regularized objectives and the rejection sampling method.
COST: 1080000
PREDICTION: This approach may improve the sample quality of the fine-tuned diffusion model, especially in cases where the denoising path is highly susceptible to noise, but may led to unexpected pattern results upon fine tuning; it might not adapt well to complex cases where variance is high, unfortunately.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with a meta-learning approach that trains the fine-tuning process itself as a neural network, taking the pre-trained diffusion model, the reward function, and the data distribution as inputs, and outputting the fine-tuned model parameters. This can be achieved by using a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) framework, where the meta-learner predicts the hyperparameters that would lead to good performance on a variety of fine-tuning tasks.
CONTROLS: We will test for different meta-learning algorithms and different fine-tuning objectives.
COST: 2880000
PREDICTION: This approach may provide a highly effective way to fine-tune diffusion models, especially in cases where the fine-tuning process needs to be highly adaptive and robust to different data distributions, but may be computationally expensive and require a large number of training samples to learn the meta-learner's parameters.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Leveraging the Generative Structure of Flow Models for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: REVISED. We will refine our previous proposal by incorporating a new component that learns to correct biases in the intermediate noisy states of the flow model using a weak signal. Specifically, we will propose a new loss function that adds a task-agnostic component that helps the model learn to compensate for distortions in the intermediate states. This can be achieved by adding a noise-adding and reconstructor component, and redefining the objective to include a matching penalty term in the latent space of the corrected flow model.
CONTROLS: The same controls as before apply, with the additional experiment testing for different strength values of the noise and different reconstructor strategies.
COST: 1080000
PREDICTION: This revised approach may provide a significant improvement over the previous version, particularly when with small changes to intermediate distributions. However, it may overfit to the bias correction task if the signal used is weak, leading to a model that is over-aligned to noisy samples of the target distribution.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Leveraging the Generative Structure of Flow Models for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: REVISED. We will fine-tune the previous revised proposal by integrating active learning and uncertainty estimation into the correction task. This will enable the model to detect situations where it is least confident in its predictions about the intermediate states, and selectively focus on correcting these. Specifically, we will add an uncertainty sampling component that selects the next set of samples that would benefit most from correction.
CONTROLS: The same controls as before apply, with the additional experiment testing for different levels of active learning and uncertainty estimation.
COST: 1620000
PREDICTION: This integrated approach may significantly improve the effectiveness of the generated states correction task by enabling the model to focus on the most problematic states, but it may lead to receiver operator characteristics degradation, as state-wise correction conditioning and otherwise-uncorrected regions may significantly reduce model reliability of state labeling operators.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Relaxed KL-Regularized PPO for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effect of relaxing the marginal KL regularization in the original KL-regularized PPO formulation for diffusion models. Specifically, we use a variational inference approach to approximate the marginal KL divergence between the pre-trained and fine-tuned distributions by bounding it with the KL divergence between the posteriors of each denoising step, rather than the entire denoising trajectories.
CONTROLS: Baseline: original KL-regularized PPO, Ablation: no KL regularization, controls the gap between fine-tuned and pre-trained model quality
COST: 500
PREDICTION: We expect a better balance between reward-maximizing and regularization, achieving higher fine-tuned model quality than the baseline with less or comparable stability issues, but potentially introducing a minor degradation in performance due to the relaxation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Using Intermediate States for Trajectory KL Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose an alternative approach to computing the trajectory KL divergence in the KL-regularized objective by approximating it with a sum of KL divergences between the posteriors of each intermediate noisy state in the denoising process and their respective reference distributions. This allows us to leverage the structure of the diffusion model by directly exploiting the conditional distributions of the intermediate states.
CONTROLS: Baseline: trajectory KL regularization, Ablation: no KL regularization, Relaxed KL-Regularized PPO (proposal 1) as an additional ablation
COST: 730.8
PREDICTION: We expect a more accurate approximation of the trajectory KL regularization, leading to finer-grained regularization and potentially better convergence towards the optimal distribution for the downstream task.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED Using Intermediate States for Trajectory KL Regularization
PROPOSAL: We modify the approximation of the trajectory KL regularization by using a variational autoencoder (VAE) to learn a low-dimensional latent representation of the intermediate noisy states, and then regularize the KL divergence between the pre-trained and fine-tuned posteriors of these latent variables, rather than directly computing it with the conditional posterior distributions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: trajectory KL regularization, Ablation: no KL regularization, Relaxed KL-Regularized PPO (proposal 1), VAE-free intermediate states approach
COST: 936
PREDICTION: We expect improved stability and efficiency in regularization, as well as better adaptability to the downstream task's data distribution, possibly resulting in higher quality fine-tuned models and more robust optimization of the reward function.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Step Flow Modulation for Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We investigate the idea of modulating the flow model's dynamics during fine-tuning by inserting reward-driven update steps into the denoising process at multiple points, with the goal of better coordinating the fine-tuning optimization with the pre-trained model's latent dynamics.
CONTROLS: Baseline: iteration-by-iteration fine-tuning, Relaxed KL-Regularized PPO (proposal 1), intermediate states approach (proposals 2)
COST: 3800
PREDICTION: We expect improved fine-tuning performance, due to the complementary learning paths established through the multi-step modulation, leading to enhanced latent representations and, consequently, better results on downstream tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rejection Sampling with Truncated Importance Sampling
PROPOSAL: We extend the rejection sampling approach for fine-tuning by applying Truncated Importance Sampling (TIS) to improve the efficiency of learning from high-reward samples. Specifically, we estimate the target distribution with a subset of high-importance samples, rather than all high-reward samples.
CONTROLS: Baseline: rejection sampling, Comparison to other rejection sampling variants (RSO, RAFT, Reinforce-Rej)
COST: 800
PREDICTION: We expect improved learning efficiency and stability, allowing for faster fine-tuning and reduction of the compute requirements for finding high-quality samples, but potentially at the cost of introducing bias in the target distribution estimate.

Note: This proposal is related to the experimental domains specified, particularly text-to-image generation, where importance sampling can be particularly effective in capturing the characteristics of high-reward samples.

TITLE: Learning a Hierarchical Prior for Regret Minimization
PROPOSAL: We address the initial value function bias problem in KL-regularized fine-tuning by learning a hierarchical prior that captures the structure of the pre-trained model's initial noise distribution. This prior serves as a regularizer, constraining the fine-tuned model's initial state to be close to the pre-trained model's, while encouraging it to make more informed decisions during the denoising process.

TITLE: Batch Normalization and Denoising Augmentation for Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose an exploration of batch normalization and denoising augmentation techniques to help diffusion models adapt to downstream tasks more effectively during fine-tuning. Specifically, we investigate the use of batch normalization to stabilize the fine-tuning process and denoising augmentation to increase the diversity of the fine-tuned model's behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Relaxed KL-Regularized PPO for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effect of relaxing the marginal KL regularization in the original KL-regularized PPO formulation for diffusion models. Specifically, we use a variational inference approach to approximate the marginal KL divergence between the pre-trained and fine-tuned distributions by bounding it with the KL divergence between the posteriors of each denoising step, rather than the entire denoising trajectories.
CONTROLS: Baseline: original KL-regularized PPO, Ablation: no KL regularization, controls the gap between fine-tuned and pre-trained model quality
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: We expect a better balance between reward-maximizing and regularization, achieving higher fine-tuned model quality than the baseline with less or comparable stability issues, but potentially introducing a minor degradation in performance due to the relaxation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Using Intermediate States for Trajectory KL Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose an alternative approach to computing the trajectory KL divergence in the KL-regularized objective by approximating it with a sum of KL divergences between the posteriors of each intermediate noisy state in the denoising process and their respective reference distributions. This allows us to leverage the structure of the diffusion model by directly exploiting the conditional distributions of the intermediate states.
CONTROLS: Baseline: trajectory KL regularization, Ablation: no KL regularization, Relaxed KL-Regularized PPO (proposal 1) as an additional ablation
COST: 2200
PREDICTION: We expect a more accurate approximation of the trajectory KL regularization, leading to finer-grained regularization and potentially better convergence towards the optimal distribution for the downstream task.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Using Intermediate States for Trajectory KL Regularization
PROPOSAL: We modify the approximation of the trajectory KL regularization by using a variational autoencoder (VAE) to learn a low-dimensional latent representation of the intermediate noisy states, and then regularize the KL divergence between the pre-trained and fine-tuned posteriors of these latent variables, rather than directly computing it with the conditional posterior distributions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: trajectory KL regularization, Ablation: no KL regularization, Relaxed KL-Regularized PPO (proposal 1), original intermediate states approach (proposal 2, before revision)
COST: 2800
PREDICTION: We expect improved stability and efficiency in regularization, as well as better adaptability to the downstream task's data distribution, possibly resulting in higher quality fine-tuned models and more robust optimization of the reward function.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the effect of KL regularization in fine-tuning diffusion models
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of fine-tuning a diffusion model on the text-to-image generation task with and without KL regularization, using the DALL-E 2 dataset and the mean squared error (MSE) as the reward function. Implement Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) as the fine-tuning algorithm, and estimate the KL divergence between the fine-tuned and pre-trained distributions using a variational inference approach.
CONTROLS: Compare against a diffusion model fine-tuned without KL regularization and against the original pre-trained model.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect the fine-tuning with KL regularization to improve the sample quality, but we worry that the KL-regularization might reduce the performance if the pre-trained model is far from the optimal distribution.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Exploring Trajectory KL Divergence Regularization for KL-Regularized Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Train a pre-trained diffusion model using the trajectory KL divergence as a suboptimal relaxation of KL regularization, specifically comparing with a KL-regularized baseline which uses a clipped KL regularizer and ignoring KL regularization. Evaluate both methods on text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation using FID score, Precision@1, and automated molecular design metrics (e.g., binding affinity).
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline: lightly fine-tuned diffusion model without regularization; (2) Ablation: baseline without KL regularization or trajectory KL divergence.

PREDICTION: Expected Results: KL-regularized fine-tuning yields better performance with controlled KL regularization, but fails to converge for complex tasks with the clipped KL regularizer; Unexpected Fail: diffusion model overcorrects due to KL regularization leading to unclustered generated samples in text-to-image generation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient-regularized activation steering for continuous control
PROPOSAL: We propose adding a gradient penalty term to the activation steering update, measured along a direction learned from contrastive examples of the target behavior. This regularizer encourages the activation update to be smooth and continuous, encouraging controlled variation of the desired behavior. We define the term as a scaled norm of the model's activation gradient along the steering direction.
CONTROLS: Compare with RMS activation steering and orthogonal projection, with and without the regularizer.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Gradient-regularized steering should provide better diffusion of control over the target behavior, resulting in smoother transitions between levels of behavior expression, while potentially degrading performance on fine-grained tasks. It might fail in tasks where small, context-dependent variations in behavior are crucial.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer Dataset: A Domestic Adversarial Testbed for LLM Evaluation
PROPOSAL: We propose developing a dataset composed of densely sampled adversarial examples of behavior manipulation in Layer family LLMs, designed to evaluate LLMs' behavior in clear-cut scenarios, with fine-grained labels marking their compliance level with the guiding behavior. To elicit and encapsulate nuances of problematic behavior in real-world data that modern corpora fail to provide, human annotators will sample instructions that command various (arguably habitual) behavior modifications. Each example contains input-output pairs of remarkably distinguishable success and failure cases of behavior compliance.
CONTROLS: Use Layer models (currently one of the leading LLM families) and our theoretical evaluations on unwilling contamination.
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: The Layer Dataset will be a valuable resource to thoroughly compare performance of superficial variants of activation steering on a constant set of tasks, both within the Layer model family and among candidates in existing literature; otherwise, demands on empirical robustness of the holistic behavior-action intervention lack a generally-pointing conjecture construct.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Activation Norm Regularization with Quantile-Normalization
PROPOSAL: We propose to incorporate an unsupervised activation norm regularization based on quantile-normalization to dynamically align layer-wise activation norms, facilitating the usage of a unified control parameter across layers. Quantile-normalization acts as an adaptive weight for sequences of samples and the same goal applies here - remodeling input distributions to guide windows of activations arriving at roughly similar levels.
CONTROLS: Investigate generalization across Layer family LLMs of varying sizes and NMT/ multi-document summarization tasks. Compare performance with the regularization from initialization and a set of neighborhood mixing of co-mass (MA) models.
COST: 18300
PREDICTION: This unsupervised regularization should alleviate the problem of non-normalized layers competing with unified hyperparameters, allowing to dramatically reduce sensitivity of the steering method to incorrect layer weights that over-did participative transformations, and simultaneously simplify control notably.

These collections enable identifying robust hyperparameter ranges by considering the model's behavior under varying tolerances for invariance loss. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of RMS Normalization on Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: We will explore how RMS normalization affects the behavior of activation steering methods and analyze their performance on a suite of benchmark datasets, including the Refusal of Harm (RoH) dataset for LLM safety. Specifically, we will study how adding, removing, or inverting a feature vector changes the model's behavior before and after RMS normalization and examine the impact of this transformation on the activation's magnitude and direction.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those of recent activation steering methods, which do not account for RMS normalization, as well as to the performance of a vanilla LLM without steering.
COST: 10
PREDICTION: We expect RMS normalization to mitigate the effects of large magnitude edits, leading to more subtle and nuanced behavior changes when inserting or removing feature vectors. However, this may come at the cost of reduced granularity, as the normalized activations may be less sensitive to the added feature. Additionally, the interaction with LLM layers may lead to unpredictable behavior, especially if the layer activation scales differ significantly. This could cause activation steering methods to fail or require additional modifications to function effectively in the context of RMS normalization.

TITLE: Suppressing Unintended Behavior by Aligning Feature Directions
PROPOSAL: We will introduce an additional alignment-based feature editing primitive that orthogonalizes the activation to the target feature direction. This is inspired by studies in psychology suggesting that behavior opposition is easier to generate when an individual faces a tangible opposing stimulus during orthogonally aligned demonstrations of action e.g. fearing candidates affiliated with duplicitous negative batteries exacerbating resistance social mimics tuổi contractions. We will investigate whether this alignment primitive can help suppress the expression of unintended behaviors, allowing for more precise control over model behavior.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to the performance of the baseline norm-constrained projection method, and examine how the combination of alignment and layer-wise normalization affects model behavior.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: We expect this alignment primitive to help reduce the likelihood of unintended behavior, particularly in scenarios where multiple target behaviors are present. However, fine-tuning the individual alignment strengths might be challenging, and the performance could degrade if the activation space contains many correlated features.

PROPOSAL: We will design and evaluate a novel emotional steering primitive that allows for controlled and nuanced emotional expression in text generation tasks. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Weighted Addition for Continuous Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: We propose to modify the activation addition primitive by introducing a learned, per-layer weight schedule. This allows for fine-tuned adaptation to the growing activation norms across layers, obviating the need for careful coefficient tuning. The weight schedule will be optimized over a validation set to achieve a balance between steering the desired behavior and preserving model coherence.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard weighted addition and directional ablation on two tasks: (i) refusal of harmful requests (e.g., challenging benchmark datasets for LLM safety) and (ii) emotion control of generated text (evaluating the influence of steering on emotional tone); use standard real-world benchmarks and datasets (e.g., SQuAD, EmoRobot), with a focus on behavioral legitimacy and coherence.
COST: 333 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: I expect Adaptive Weighted Addition to outperform standard addition in terms of steerability and coherence, especially for strong steering demands. However, it might still not capture the full complexity of the model's behavior under light steering.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spherical Embeddings of Steering Directions
PROPOSAL: We investigate how the RMS normalization of activations influences the steering operations, introducing a novel hypothesis: the steering directions, typically represented as vectors in high-dimensional activation space, should be reparameterized to lie on the surface of a unit sphere. This geometric interpretation facilitates a theoretically grounded treatment of how different steering operations interact and control for behaviors. Furthermore, we propose using techniques from spherical geometry, such as the Hopf fibration, to explore the relationship between steering directions and activations.
CONTROLS: Examining how standard activation-steering operations perform on the reparameterized representation, and conducting an analysis of their respective effects and limitations under RMS-normalization. Controls include standard addition and ablation without normalization (orthogonalized additions for fairness) and a high-dimensional invariance analysis of LLM models trained on diverse real-world data.
COST: 832 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results should reveal significant distortions and unexplored capabilities of standard steering operations, and demonstrate the utility of considering activations in the complex, spherical geometry typically induced by normalization. However, the Hopf-fibration regularization might not achieve significant, independent real-world performance gains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Directional Projection Regularization
PROPOSAL: Building on our spherical embeddings hypothesis, we introduce a new steering operation: rotational projection regularization. By projecting activations onto a range of steering directions, each associated with a distinct behavior, and combining elementwise the resulting projections, we can encourage or reinforce specific responses while modulating the influence of other behaviors. We propose tuning the steering coefficients to adjust the magnitude of the selected behavior, thus offering a more differentiated control over the expression of behaviors.
CONTROLS: Baseline comparisons with Adaptive Weighted Addition (proposal 1), standard weighted addition (with careful tuning of coefficients), and a rigorous inversion analysis to avoid misencoding or double suppression of undesirable behaviors. Validate on emotion control tasks across emotion detection datasets.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: I expect rotational projection regularization to demonstrate superior steerability and control, and achieve significant performance gains in targeted steering of LLMs across tasks. However, the interactive relationship between steering directions may necessitate fine-tuning across different LLM models and training conditions to ensure optimal behavior suppression or reinforcement.

By projecting activations onto a range of steering directions, each associated with a distinct behavior, and combining elementwise the resulting projections, we can encourage or reinforce specific responses while modulating the influence of other behaviors. We propose tuning the steering coefficients to adjust the magnitude of the selected behavior, thus offering a more differentiated control over the expression of behaviors.
CONTROLS: Baseline comparisons with Adaptive Weighted Addition (proposal 1), standard weighted addition (with careful tuning of coefficients), and a rigorous inversion analysis to avoid misencoding or double suppression of undesirable behaviors. Validate on emotion control tasks across emotion detection datasets.
COST: 13500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: I expect rotational projection regularization to demonstrate superior steerability and control, and achieve significant performance gains in targeted steering of LLMs across tasks. However, the interactive relationship between steering directions may necessitate fine-tuning across different LLM models and training conditions to ensure optimal behavior suppression or reinforcement.

TITLE: Adaptive Weighted Addition for Continuous Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: We propose to modify the activation addition primitive by introducing a learned, per-layer weight schedule. This allows for fine-tuned adaptation to the growing activation norms across layers, obviating the need for careful coefficient tuning. The weight schedule will be optimized over a validation set to achieve a balance between steering the desired behavior and preserving model coherence.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard weighted addition and directional ablation on two tasks: (i) refusal of harmful requests (e.g., challenging benchmark datasets for LLM safety) and (ii) emotion control of generated text (evaluating the influence of steering on emotional tone); use standard real-world benchmarks and datasets (e.g., SQuAD, EmoRobot), with a focus on behavioral legitimacy and coherence.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: I expect Adaptive Weighted Addition to outperform standard addition in terms of steerability and coherence, especially for strong steering demands. However, it might still not capture the full complexity of the model's behavior under light steering.

TITLE: Spherical Embeddings of Steering Directions
PROPOSAL: We investigate how the RMS normalization of activations influences the steering operations, introducing a novel hypothesis: the steering directions, typically represented as vectors in high-dimensional activation space, should be reparameterized to lie on the surface of a unit sphere. This geometric interpretation facilitates a theoretically grounded treatment of how different steering operations interact and control for behaviors. Furthermore, we propose using techniques from spherical geometry, such as the Hopf fibration, to explore the relationship between steering directions and activations.
CONTROLS: Examining how standard activation-steering operations perform on the reparameterized representation, and conducting an analysis of their respective effects and limitations under RMS-normalization. COST: 2500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Results should reveal significant distortions and unexplored capabilities of standard steering operations, and demonstrate the utility of considering activations in the complex, spherical geometry typically induced by normalization. However, the Hopf-fibration regularization might not achieve significant, independent real-world performance gains.

TITLE: Generalized Conditional Steering
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate a generalized conditional steering approach that combines the strengths of activation addition and directional ablation. Specifically, we will estimate a feature direction and its negation, apply a weighted sum to mix the two primitive operations, and schedule these weights according to a simple, learnable control parameter. This approach allows for more flexible and adaptive steering while maintaining interpretability.
CONTROLS: baseline is model behavior without steering; ablate the control parameter learning component; compare to conditional versions of activation addition and directional ablation.

PREDICTION: Conditional steering will provide more flexible and expressive control over the model behavior, as it can leverage both positive and negative alignments with the feature direction. This should help bridge the gap between fine-grained and coarse-grained steering, and experiments should reveal gradual, rather than abrupt, changes in behavior as steering strength varies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Canonical Steering Primitives for Fine-Grained Control
PROPOSAL: We will compare the existing activation addition and directional ablation primitives on a benchmark of tasks involving refusal of harmful requests and emotion control in generated text, using different languages and model sizes. Specifically, we will train and test RoBERTa and Long-Tails models on the crowd-sourced List of Harmlss Words (LHW) and the Affective Norms for English Words (ANEW) datasets. Steering performance will be evaluated using metrics like accuracy, fluency, and incoherence rates.
CONTROLS: ablate each primitive individually, with no steering; compare to a conditional version of each primitive applied selectively.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Activation addition will struggle to provide fine-grained control, with sharp cutoffs and failure to induce partial suppression or inversion due to layer specificity of activation scales. Directional ablation will be more successful, but its tendency to ignore negative alignment may lead to coarser control than desired.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Model Behavior under RMS Normalization
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of RMS normalization on the steering primitives, using a simulation where we normalize the activation spaces of large language models (LLMs) and evaluate the resulting behavior under activation addition and directional ablation. Specifically, we will take the pre-training data of a RoBERTa and Long-Tails model, normalize the activation spaces, and apply various steering edits to measure their effectiveness and robustness across different tasks.
CONTROLS: compare to baseline (unnormalized) activations.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: We expect to find that RMS normalization has a noticeable impact on the steering primitives, causing them to behave differently (e.g., becoming more sensitive to coefficient values) and interact with other features encoded in the same representation, but the exact effects will depend on the specific model architecture and training regime.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generalized Conditional Steering
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate a generalized conditional steering approach that combines the strengths of activation addition and directional ablation. Specifically, we will estimate a feature direction and its negation, apply a weighted sum to mix the two primitive operations, and schedule these weights according to a simple, learnable control parameter. This approach allows for more flexible and adaptive steering while maintaining interpretability.
CONTROLS: baseline is model behavior without steering; ablate the control parameter learning component; compare to conditional versions of activation addition and directional ablation.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: Conditional steering will provide more flexible and expressive control over the model behavior, as it can leverage both positive and negative alignments with the feature direction. This should help bridge the gap between fine-grained and coarse-grained steering, and experiments should reveal gradual, rather than abrupt, changes in behavior as steering strength varies.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating Canonical Steering Primitives with Task-Specific Projections
PROPOSAL: We will extend the evaluation of canonical steering primitives (Proposal 1) by incorporating task-specific projections that aim to align the feature direction with the target behavior. These projections will be learned via backpropagation and help to reduce the dependence on layer-specific activation scales, enabling more consistent steering across different parts of the model.
CONTROLS: compare to baseline without task-specific projections; ablate the backpropagation-based learning component.
COST: 5200
PREDICTION: The task-specific projections should improve the performance of activation addition by allowing for more targeted and interpretable steering, and enabling finer-grained control. Directional ablation should also benefit from this change, although its coarser control tendencies will likely persist.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Layer-Specific Activation Scales in Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: Compare the accuracy and fluency of activation addition and ablation for steering LLMs, and analyze the relationship between layer-specific activation scales and steering performance on the 2021 LAMA conversational AI dataset [13]. Utilize the ViLBERT [16] model and evaluate the two steering primitives with and without norm-normalized coefficients, adjusting the coefficient for each layer separately as well as globally.
CONTROLS: Baselines include a standard LAMA model and two ablated models where one or both steering operations have been removed, as well as a norm-normalized addition baseline with a fixed, globally shared coefficient.
COST: 10080
PREDICTION: We expect steering to be more challenging for deep layers, but the correct adjustment of layer-specific coefficients may partially mitigate this issue. Image-sentence pairing reasoning might be less sensitive to coefficients' mismatch.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncovering LLM Behavior via Activations' Orthogonal Projections
PROPOSAL: Develop a new visualization tool, activation inspection, to better understand how model behaviors get encoded in activation space. This involves projecting individual activations onto a low-dimensional space, preserving their directions but compressing their magnitudes along an orthogonal feature direction of interest, and visualizing the resulting embeddings with t-SNE [14]. We will test this on 500 dialogue turns from the recently-released ' Bengal and Indo-British Army puts down militia in Chittagong Hill Tracts' Wikipedia article, exploring the contrast between an affirmative and a contemporaneous refusal of an explicit harmful request.
CONTROLS: Include baselines for random projections and a model that has not been steered, as well as evaluation of the method's sensitivity to the choice of the orthogonal feature direction.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: Activation inspection can offer valuable insights into the activation space landscape, providing clear visual cues for when seemingly disparate behaviors align with a common underlying feature, even if our current steering operations are oblivious to these patterns and struggle to capture their essence. However, results might be less clear cut when cases involve diffuse or emergent behaviors.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Continuous Activation Steering via Hypernetwork-Layer Interactions (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Update the hypernetwork-layer interaction approach to better account for layer-specific activation scales and RMS normalization. This involves designing a hierarchical hypernetwork structure, where each hypernetwork node is associated with a specific layer and is trained to modulate the corresponding activation scale. Furthermore, we incorporate a regularization term to encourage the hypernetwork to learn layer-specific adjustment coefficients that are consistent with the model's original training regimen and RMS normalization. This will help the hypernetwork to better navigate the trade-off between steering performance and model coherence. 
CONTROLS: Include baselines for standard activation addition and ablation, as well as a variant of the hypernetwork-layer interaction approach without regularization.
COST: 82000
PREDICTION: The revised hypernetwork-layer interaction approach should provide more accurate and coherent steering results, and its regularized version should achieve better convergence to optimal steering coefficients. However, it may require more computational resources due to the increased complexity of the hypernetwork structure.

PROPOSAL: Develop a new visualization tool, activation inspection, to better understand how model behaviors get encoded in activation space. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Model Heterogeneity: A Baseline
PROPOSAL: We will implement a naive baseline for federated multi-task learning with model heterogeneity by using existing federated multi-task learning methods (e.g., FedBMAdaPT [1]) that require users to have the same model architecture and train them separately for each task. This baseline will serve as a reference point for future experiments. We will consider various configurations, including using different pre-trained foundation models for each task and evaluating personalized models' performance on unseen test data.
CONTROLS: FedBMAdaPT with different model architectures; server-side ensemble of individual models
COST: 15
PREDICTION: This baseline will likely perform well on single-task settings but fail to generalize across multiple tasks due to its inability to capture cross-task information.

TITLE: Enhancing Federated Multi-Task Learning with Model-Agnostic Loss Functions
PROPOSAL: We will extend the baseline model (FedBMAdaPT) by replacing its loss functions with several model-agnostic variants, including the Proximal Loss based on Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) [2] and the symmetric InfoNCE loss with a Gram matrix. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gramian-Based Contrastive Loss for Joint Alignment of Multiple Model Representations
PROPOSAL: We will propose a new Gramian-based contrastive loss for jointly aligning the representations produced by an arbitrary number of models, surpassing existing pairwise alignment methods (e.g., InfoNCE). This loss function aims to capture the dependencies among all representations by computing a Gram matrix and encouraging it to be close to a theoretically grounded ideal Gram matrix.
CONTROLS: Benchmark against state-of-the-art pairwise alignment methods (e.g., InfoNCE); comparative analysis on synthetic and real-world datasets
COST: 35
PREDICTION: The proposed Gramian-based contrastive loss may significantly improve the alignment of multiple model representations, leading to better cross-task performance and knowledge transfer, and may also have a positive impact on privacy as the number of shared parameters is reduced.

TITLE: Adaptive Federated Multi-Task Learning with Dynamic Model Architecture Selection
PROPOSAL: We will propose an adaptive federated multi-task learning framework that dynamically selects the model architecture for each user based on their local data and task requirements. This framework will be implemented using a reinforcement learning approach, where the model architecture selection is treated as a Markov decision process, and the goal is to optimize the trade-off between model performance and communication overhead.
CONTROLS: Baseline models with pre-specified model architectures; existing federated multi-task learning methods with fixed model architectures

TITLE: Multi-Task Federated Learning with Group Sparsity Regularization
PROPOSAL: We will propose a multi-task federated learning method that incorporates group sparsity regularization to encourage sharing of common features across tasks, while also allowing for task-specific features. This method will be implemented using a group Lasso approach, where the shared and task-specific features are treated as separate groups, and the L1 norm is applied to each group.
CONTROLS: Baseline models without group sparsity regularization; existing federated multi-task learning methods with either no sparsity regularization or task-specific regularization
COST: 54
PREDICTION: This proposal may lead to improved knowledge transfer and better alignment of features across tasks, as well as the ability to capture task-specific patterns, but may also come with a higher computational cost due to the group Lasso regularizer.

TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning with Arbitrary Architectures and Tasks
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to federated multi-task learning that allows users with heterogeneous architectures and tasks to collaboratively improve their models without requiring any architectural congruity. Our method, called "Meta-Alignment," utilizes a meta-learning framework to align the representations of multiple models in a shared space, using a combination of centered kernel alignment and a novel gramian-based loss. This alignment is performed on a small public dataset, allowing for efficient knowledge transfer across tasks. Additionally, we propose a task-agnostic prediction module that enables each user's model to leverage the shared representation space for improved generalization.
CONTROLS: We compare our method to existing federated multi-task learning methods, including recent divide-and-conquer approaches that assume homogeneous architectures. We also include baselines that utilize knowledge distillation and contrastive learning, as well as a model-agnostic approach that adds a proximal term based on centered kernel alignment.
COST: 53,123,000
PREDICTION: Our results show that Meta-Alignment significantly outperforms existing methods across a range of real-world tasks, including image classification, language modeling, and sentiment analysis. However, the performance of our method may suffer when users have significantly different task distributions or when the public dataset is too small to accurately capture the shared representation space.

TITLE: Flexible Federated Multi-Task Learning with Adaptive Weighted Contrastive Loss
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a flexible federated multi-task learning framework that learns an adaptive weighted contrastive loss based on the representations from all users. Specifically, we will use a neural network to predict the importance of each contrastive term and dynamically adjust the weights of different terms during federated training. This will allow our framework to adapt to the specific scenario and align representations that are more relevant for each client's task. We will evaluate our approach on the CIFAR100, IMDB, and 20Newsgroups datasets, where clients have different model architectures and perform different tasks.
CONTROLS: Pairwise Contrastive Loss, Pure Federated Learning, Center-based method
COST: 6700
PREDICTION: Our approach should be robust to diverse client architectures and tasks, but might suffer from overfitting to the importance prediction network.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Federated Multi-Task Learning with Pairwise Contrastive Loss
PROPOSAL: We propose to perform federated multi-task learning with a pairwise contrastive loss that aligns the representations between all pairs of models. This will be done on the CIFAR100 dataset, where each client has a different architecture and performs a different task. We will use a Seasong Rachael TF Hub pre-trained model as the backbone, fine-tune it on local data, and then perform federated semi-supervised learning with our proposed pairwise contrastive loss and a center-based method as baseline.
CONTROLS: Center-based method, Pure Federated Learning (no contrastive loss)
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: This approach should work reasonably well for the CIFAR100 dataset, but will struggle with datasets having different numbers of classes, as the pairwise contrastive loss is not class-aware.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flexible Federated Multi-Task Learning with Adaptive Weighted Contrastive Loss
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a flexible federated multi-task learning framework that learns an adaptive weighted contrastive loss based on the representations from all users. Specifically, we will use a neural network to predict the importance of each contrastive term and dynamically adjust the weights of different terms during federated training. This will allow our framework to adapt to the specific scenario and align representations that are more relevant for each client's task. We will evaluate our approach on the CIFAR100, IMDB, and 20Newsgroups datasets, where clients have different model architectures and perform different tasks.
CONTROLS: Pairwise Contrastive Loss, Pure Federated Learning, Center-based method
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: Our approach should be robust to diverse client architectures and tasks, but might suffer from overfitting to the importance prediction network.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gramian-Based Representational Alignment for Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the use of Gramian-based representational alignment in federated multi-task learning. We will apply a recently proposed Gramian-based contrastive loss to align representations from all clients simultaneously, without pairwise contrastive losses. This approach, when combined with federated semi-supervised learning, will be tested on the 20Newsgroups and IMDB datasets, where clients have different model architectures and perform text classification tasks. We will also compare against the pairwise contrastive loss and pure federated learning as baselines.
CONTROLS: Pairwise Contrastive Loss, Pure Federated Learning
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: Gramian-based alignment might provide a good balance between expressive power and stability, but the lack of theoretical justification in prior work raises concerns about its robustness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theory of Representational Alignment in Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: Building on Gramian-based contrastive losses, we develop a theoretical framework to analyze the convergence of representational alignment in federated learning. Specifically, we will provide a set of sufficient conditions under which the Gramian-based loss guarantees the alignment of representations in a shared representation space. We will assume i.i.d. data distributed across clients and use the error feedback method to tackle non-i.i.d. data. We will provide theoretical bounds on the convergence rate of the Gramian-based loss under the assumptions.
CONTROLS: Empirical evaluation of Gramian-based loss, baseline (random initialization)
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: Our theoretical framework might provide strong guarantees under ideal conditions, but the resulting bounds would likely be loose and there might be large experimental gaps between the theoretical results and real-world performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REFINE: Pairwise Contrastive Loss for Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We refine our previous pairwise contrastive loss proposal to use a more advanced metric to compare representations. Instead of using the standard dot product, we use cosine similarity on different layers of the models to compute the contrastive loss. This will allow our framework to capture more nuanced differences in the representations and align them more accurately. We will re-evaluate our approach on the FEMNIST dataset, 20Newsgroups and IMDB datasets, where clients have different model architectures and perform different handwritten digit classification, text classification and language modeling tasks.
CONTROLS: Original pairwise contrastive loss, Center-based method, No contrastive loss
COST: 22000
PREDICTION: Our refined pairwise contrastive loss should improve performance over the original loss, especially in datasets with different types of data, but it may be more computationally intensive.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Federated Multi-Task Learning with Pairwise Contrastive Loss
PROPOSAL: We refine our previous pairwise contrastive loss proposal to focus on aligning representations that are most relevant for each client's task. Specifically, we will use an attention mechanism to dynamically weight the importance of each client's representation when computing the contrastive loss. This will allow our framework to adapt to the specific scenario and align representations that are most relevant for each client's task. We will re-evaluate our approach on the CIFAR100 and IMDB datasets, where clients have different model architectures and perform different tasks.
CONTROLS: Original pairwise contrastive loss, Center-based method, Pure Federated Learning
COST: 25000
PREDICTION: Our refined pairwise contrastive loss should improve performance over the original loss, especially in datasets with different tasks, but it may be sensitive to the choice of attention mechanism.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploiting Task Relationships for Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose to explore the use of task relationships to improve federated multi-task learning. Specifically, we will model the relationships between tasks as a Gaussian process and use this to regularize the contrastive loss. We will evaluate our approach on the 20Newsgroups, IMDB, and CIFAR100 datasets, where clients have different model architectures and perform different tasks.
CONTROLS: Pure Federated Learning, baseline (average task loss)
COST: 28000
PREDICTION: Our approach should improve performance over baseline models by leveraging task relationships, but may be sensitive to the choice of task relationship model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Heterogeneous Model Architectures in Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate the use of pre-trained models as a shared knowledge source for federated multi-task learning. Specifically, we will use a frozen pre-trained model as an initialization for the local models in each client, and then fine-tune the pre-trained model in a federated manner. We will evaluate our approach on the IMDB, 20Newsgroups, and CIFAR100 datasets, where clients have different model architectures and perform different tasks.
CONTROLS: Pure Federated Learning, without pre-trained model initialization
COST: 32000
PREDICTION: Our approach should improve performance over baseline models by leveraging pre-trained knowledge, but may be sensitive to the choice of pre-trained model and the level of fine-tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Communication-Efficient Federated Multi-Task Learning with Adaptive Cluster Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a communication-efficient federated multi-task learning framework that adaptively selects a cluster of clients to participate in each round of federated training. Specifically, we will use a clustering algorithm to group clients with similar task distributions, and then randomly sample clients from each cluster to participate in federated training. We will evaluate our approach on the CIFAR100 and IMDB datasets, where clients have different model architectures and perform different tasks.
CONTROLS: Pure Federated Learning, baseline (random client sampling)
COST: 38000
PREDICTION: Our approach should improve communication efficiency while maintaining performance, but may be sensitive to the choice of clustering algorithm and the number of clusters.

TITLE: Federated Adaptation with Instance Alignments
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we propose a federated adaptation approach that aligns instance-level representations across users with heterogeneous model architectures and tasks. We modify the InfoNCE loss to learn an alignment function that groups similar instances across users, rather than aligning pairs of models.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach with existing methods for federated multi-task learning, such as MoCo and KDA, on datasets such as CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and PubMed.
COST: 1670
PREDICTION: Our approach should outperform existing methods in terms of instance-level similarity and task performance on standard benchmarks. However, it may struggle with cases where the tasks have very different instance distributions.

Next steps include exploring how to learn a grouping function based on representation similarity and how to aggregate and refine the instance-level alignments across users and tasks.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Heterogeneous Task Embeddings for Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we propose a method that learns task-agnostic representations of heterogeneous tasks as embeddings in a shared space. We train a multi-task neural network with a task embedding loss that minimizes the similarity between task embeddings with dissimilar task performance. This allows for knowledge sharing between tasks without requiring model congruity.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method with existing methods for federated multi-task learning, such as FedMTL and MoCo, on datasets such as STL-10, Caltech-101, and ImageNet.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Our proposed method should capture task relationships and promote knowledge sharing between tasks. However, it may struggle with highly dissimilar tasks that require distinct architectures.

Turn 2 Experiments:

1. Federated Adaptation with Instance Alignments
2. Heterogeneous Task Embeddings for Federated Multi-Task Learning

Next steps include investigating the impact of task embedding dimensionality and the trade-off between task similarity and model discrepancy.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Multi-Task Learning via Quadratic Wasserstein Barycenter
PROPOSAL: In this theoretical result, we provide a model-agnostic framework for multi-task learning via quadratic Wasserstein barycenter, which minimizes the difference in quadratic costs between users and tasks while preserving the geometric structure of the data. This approach ensures that users can choose arbitrary architectures and local datasets without requiring model congruity or paired representations.
CONTROLS: We will provide a preliminary analysis of the computational complexity and convergence rate of our proposed method under specific conditions.
COST: 2850
PREDICTION: Our proposed method should provide a principled way to learn shared representations across users with heterogeneous architectures and tasks, and handle model disagreement and distribution mismatch. However, it may require efficient implementation and a large number of training iterations.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Practical Federated Learning with Mechanism Design for Data Provenance
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we introduce a mechanism design framework to ensure data provenance and accountability in federated learning. We propose a data protection mechanism that selectively exposes data to preserve user privacy, and tune a learning algorithm under this constraint to achieve optimal utility. Our approach is designed to be practical and scalable, leveraging existing optimization techniques and leveraging the strengths of federated learning.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach with existing federated learning methods that prioritize user privacy, such as differential privacy and homomorphic encryption, on datasets such as LinkedIn and health data, and evaluate the impact of data exposure on classification accuracy.
COST: 3700
PREDICTION: Our mechanism design approach should improve the practicality and scalability of federated learning while preserving user privacy and data accountability.

TITLE: Global-Scale Federated Learning with Distributed Clustering and Truncated Bayesian Optimization

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Heterogeneous Federated Multi-Task Learning with Asymmetric Transfer
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a novel heterogeneous federated multi-task learning method, combining knowledge distillation with asymmetric transfer. Each user exchanges task-specific outputs with a global controller, which generates a guidance signal based on the collective knowledge from other users. The guidance signal serves as an auxiliary task and is projected onto the local task-specific predictor of the user under consideration. We employ a source-sensitive weight mechanism that automatically adapts the importance for each individual user's model when computing the collective knowledge, considering both their contribution and similarity in the learned representations.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) apply knowledge distillation with source-sensitive weight to three pre-trained foundation models with distinct architectures on three real-world classification tasks from the Heterogeneous Federated Learning Tasks datasets; (2) optimize the mechanism under evaluation using an extensive grid search method and analyze the procedure. Asymmetric transfer share knowledge between users in implementations without InfoNCE based representation learning.
CONTROLS: Federated KL and Conditional knowledge transfer baselines; source-sensitive weight ablation
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: we expect significant improvements compared to existing methods with reduced training time and increased interconnected system stability when the models used have starkly differing architectures; this method's performance may diminish when knowledge is highly unevenly distributed among users.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: FedRep: Gramian-based Contrastive Learning for Multi-Task Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: 
Introduce FedRep, a theoretically grounded Gramian-based contrastive loss that aligns representations from multiple models. FedRep jointly captures the dependencies among the representations by applying a quadratic kernel on their concatenation, rather than relying on pairwise alignments. This allows for effective transfer of knowledge across tasks and between models with arbitrary architectures and different modalities. We prove that FedRep preserves structural properties of the data and aligns representations in a way that generalizes well to novel tasks.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) compare FedRep with pairwise alignment-based methods on five federated learning tasks with different modalities from the OMNIGLOT, CIFAR10 and MNIST benchmark datasets; (2) explore FedRep's transferability across multiple task spaces and show that heterogeneous generalization can be improved.
CONTROLS: InfoNCE loss with all pairs of users; federated self-supervised methods
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: expect FedRep to achieve state-of-the-art results and improve cross-task transfer with guaranteed convergence to a known and demure region of pre-defined mineable stable knowledge; limited improvement might be expected in smaller or less diverse data streams.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Modified Title and Proposal: FedRep - Enhanced Gramian-based Contrastive Learning for Multi-Task Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: 
Modify FedRep to incorporate a proximal term to further improve the generalization and transferability of the aligned representations. The proximal term adds a localized regularization effect and also helps in dimensionality reduction. We also modify the kernel used in FedRep to allow for more flexibility in incorporating different types of data modalities and their associated complexities. This is achieved by adapting the Gaussian RBF kernel to be modulated by an adaptive scaling factor computed based on the uncertainty in each model's representation. We prove the theoretical soundness of the method under moderate assumption on the data structure.
ALLOCATIONS: compare the modified FedRep with existing pairwise alignment and proxy-based methods for heterogeneous federated multi-task learning on five benchmark datasets; evaluate the role of modulated kernel functions in facilitating shared representation generalization between models with diverse modalities.
CONTROLS: InfoNCE loss with partial sets of user pairs; distillation-based relevance loss
COST: 7308
PREDICTION: Expect the modified FedRep to consistently outperform prior methods for comprehensive model-sharing; significantly enhanced task concordance can be prohibited by issues of inappropriate generalizability.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Low-Rank Adaptation for Multi-Task Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a low-rank adaptation method for heterogeneous federated multi-task learning. We propose to incorporate a low-rank factorization into the heterogeneity-aware federated learning framework. Each user's model consists of a shared low-rank layer and task-specific layers. We employ a low-rank factorization trick on the shared layer, promoting effective knowledge transfer among users while reducing the risk of overfitting under heterogeneous model architectures. This framework is further enhanced by introducing a centroid-driven method to adapt the client's local model to the global server.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) evaluate the proposed method on three large-scale multi-task learning datasets under scenarios with a varying number of tasks and users; (2) compare the performance with other competitive low-rank federated learning methods.
CONTROLS: a centroid-based adaptation with InfoNCE loss; heterogeneity-aware federated learning framework with Baseline adaptation
COST: 8320
PREDICTION: Expect our low-rank adaptation method to improve communication efficiency while significantly enhancing knowledge transfer and mitigating model disparity; knowledge transfer might decrease with increasing model difference and super-parameter heterogeneity.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Model Collaborative Representation Learning through Mutual Information Maximization
PROPOSAL: 
Introduce a novel approach for heterogeneous federated multi-task learning that maximizes mutual information between the learned representations of multiple models. By optimizing the mutual information between latent representations, our framework encourages an efficient sharing and alignment of valuable information across models. This approach enables the exploration of complex dependencies among representations without assuming model congruity. The proposal consists of two building blocks: a graph-based neural network architecture for representing task relationships and a innovative pointwise mutual information (PMI) estimator for estimating mutual information between task-specific representations.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework on tasks with varying difficulty and complexity levels; (2) compare the performance with competing heterogeneous federated learning approaches such as asymmetric transfer and low-rank adaptation.
CONTROLS: asymmetric transfer with InfoNCE loss; independent model optimization with Proximal Term
COST: 10657.71
PREDICTION: We anticipate improvement in knowledge transfer over existing approaches and increased stability in model collaboration; limitations may be caused by existing biases in the optimization process.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Efficient Federated Learning with Shared-Aware Model Pruning
PROPOSAL: 
Develop an efficient heterogeneous federated learning algorithm that utilizes shared-aware model pruning. Our approach leverages a smart pruning framework, where each user optimizes both model pruning and knowledge distillation simultaneously. By reducing the model size, we not only decrease the communication cost but also improve the sharing and learning efficiency of shared representations for federated learning. Furthermore, We propose a novel shared-aware pruning criterion which adaptively identifies and prunes less important weights across shared layers of multiple models, effectively accelerating the convergence of heterogeneous federated learning.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) experimentally demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed framework using various resources constraints; (2) compare with heterogeneous federated learning methods that do not incorporate knowledge distillation.
CONTROLS: prune-based knowledge distillation without knowledge distillation loss; asynchronous federated edge learning
COST: 13318.4
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the proposed method greatly improves efficiency, in terms of communication cost, computation time, and memory usage, especially when handling heterogeneous models with diverse complexities and scales; performance may degrade under high pruning ratios or with highly sparse training data.

Develop a comprehensive and unified framework that integrates the strengths of various heterogeneous federated multi-task learning methods. By combining techniques from robustness, generalization, and model personalization, our framework offers a versatile solution for learning from diverse data and heterogeneous user tasks. We rigorously evaluate the proposed framework using extensive benchmarking and provide insights into the trade-offs between different components.

TITLE: Heterogeneous Federated Multi-Task Learning with Asymmetric Transfer
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a novel heterogeneous federated multi-task learning method, combining knowledge distillation with asymmetric transfer. Each user exchanges task-specific outputs with a global controller, which generates a guidance signal based on the collective knowledge from other users. The guidance signal serves as an auxiliary task and is projected onto the local task-specific predictor of the user under consideration. We employ a source-sensitive weight mechanism that automatically adapts the importance for each individual user's model when computing the collective knowledge, considering both their contribution and similarity in the learned representations.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) apply knowledge distillation with source-sensitive weight to three pre-trained foundation models with distinct architectures on three real-world classification tasks from the Heterogeneous Federated Learning Tasks datasets; (2) optimize the mechanism under evaluation using an extensive grid search method and analyze the procedure. ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: FedRep: Gramian-based Contrastive Learning for Multi-Task Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: 
Introduce FedRep, a theoretically grounded Gramian-based contrastive loss that aligns representations from multiple models. FedRep jointly captures the dependencies among the representations by applying a quadratic kernel on their concatenation, rather than relying on pairwise alignments. This allows for effective transfer of knowledge across tasks and between models with arbitrary architectures and different modalities. We prove that FedRep preserves structural properties of the data and aligns representations in a way that generalizes well to novel tasks.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) compare FedRep with pairwise alignment-based methods on five federated learning tasks with different modalities from the OMNIGLOT, CIFAR10 and MNIST benchmark datasets; (2) explore FedRep's transferability across multiple task spaces and show that heterogeneous generalization can be improved.
CONTROLS: InfoNCE loss with all pairs of users; federated self-supervised methods
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: expect FedRep to achieve state-of-the-art results and improve cross-task transfer with guaranteed convergence to a known and demure region of pre-defined mineable stable knowledge; limited improvement might be expected in smaller or less diverse data streams.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Modified Title and Proposal: FedRep - Enhanced Gramian-based Contrastive Learning for Multi-Task Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: 
Modify FedRep to incorporate a proximal term to further improve the generalization and transferability of the aligned representations. The proximal term adds a localized regularization effect and also helps in dimensionality reduction. We also modify the kernel used in FedRep to allow for more flexibility in incorporating different types of data modalities and their associated complexities. This is achieved by adapting the Gaussian RBF kernel to be modulated by an adaptive scaling factor computed based on the uncertainty in each model's representation. We prove the theoretical soundness of the method under moderate assumption on the data structure.

TITLE: Low-Rank Adaptation for Multi-Task Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: 
Develop a low-rank adaptation method for heterogeneous federated multi-task learning. We propose to incorporate a low-rank factorization into the heterogeneity-aware federated learning framework. Each user's model consists of a shared low-rank layer and task-specific layers. We employ a low-rank factorization trick on the shared layer, promoting effective knowledge transfer among users while reducing the risk of overfitting under heterogeneous model architectures. This framework is further enhanced by introducing a centroid-driven method to adapt the client's local model to the global server.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) evaluate the proposed method on three large-scale multi-task learning datasets under scenarios with a varying number of tasks and users; (2) compare the performance with other competitive low-rank federated learning methods.
CONTROLS: a centroid-based adaptation with InfoNCE loss; heterogeneity-aware federated learning framework with Baseline adaptation
COST: 25000
PREDICTION: Expect our low-rank adaptation method to improve communication efficiency while significantly enhancing knowledge transfer and mitigating model disparity; knowledge transfer might decrease with increasing model difference and super-parameter heterogeneity.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Model Collaborative Representation Learning through Mutual Information Maximization
PROPOSAL: 
Introduce a novel approach for heterogeneous federated multi-task learning that maximizes mutual information between the learned representations of multiple models. By optimizing the mutual information between latent representations, our framework encourages an efficient sharing and alignment of valuable information across models. This approach enables the exploration of complex dependencies among representations without assuming model congruity. The proposal consists of two building blocks: a graph-based neural network architecture for representing task relationships and a innovative pointwise mutual information (PMI) estimator for estimating mutual information between task-specific representations.
ALLOCATIONS: (1) empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework on tasks with varying difficulty and complexity levels; (2) compare the performance with competing heterogeneous federated learning approaches such as asymmetric transfer and low-rank adaptation.
CONTROLS: asymmetric transfer with InfoNCE loss; independent model optimization with Proximal Term
COST: 32000
PREDICTION: We anticipate improvement in knowledge transfer over existing approaches and increased stability in model collaboration; limitations may be caused by existing biases in the optimization process.

PROPOSAL: 
Develop an efficient heterogeneous federated learning algorithm that utilizes shared-aware model pruning. Our approach leverages a smart pruning framework, where each user optimizes both model pruning and knowledge distillation simultaneously. By reducing the model size, we not only decrease the communication cost but also improve the sharing and learning efficiency of shared representations for federated learning. Furthermore, We propose a novel shared-aware pruning criterion which adaptively identifies and prunes less important weights across shared layers of multiple models, effectively accelerating the convergence of heterogeneous federated learning.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE:  Active Label Correction with Reinforcement Learning
PROPOSAL:  Experiment: Implement a reinforcement learning framework to actively explore different label correction possibilities and learn from long-term consequences of its decisions on noisy classification datasets. Specifically, we'll use a model-based reinforcement learning approach to select a subset of training samples to correct, based on their potential impact on model generalization. We'll use Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) as the reinforcement learning algorithm and train a model to select samples that maximize the expected improvement in model accuracy. We'll evaluate this framework on several real-world noisy datasets, including CIFAR-10 with 20% label noise and ImageNet with 5% label noise.
CONTROLS:  Baseline comparisons with existing state-of-the-art label correction methods, including SMOTE and EasyEnsemble, as well as a naive approach that always corrects the most uncertain samples.
COST:  1440
PREDICTION:  Expected result: Active label correction with reinforcement learning can lead to significant improvements in model accuracy on noisy datasets, potentially up to 10%. However, its performance may degrade if the model overestimates the impact of correcting individual samples, leading to inefficient exploration.
