TITLE: Exploring Iterative Label Correction with Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Regularization
PROPOSAL: We design a method called "CorrEnsemble" that combines label correction and ensemble regularization techniques to iteratively refine the noisy labels. CorrEnsemble utilizes a novel variant of the state-of-the-art Mixup loss formulation that incorporates uncertainty-aware weights based on the predictions of a deep neural network ensemble. This allows the model to adaptively explore different label correction possibilities and learn from the long-term consequences of its decisions.
CONTROLS: We consider two strong baselines: 1) a standard neural network trained on the noisy labels without label correction and 2) an active learning-based approach that uses prediction loss and confidence levels to isolate and manage noisy labels. We also include an ablation study to evaluate the effect of the uncertainty-aware weights on the overall performance.
COST: 51000
PREDICTION: CorrEnsemble should show significant improvements over the baselines in terms of accuracy and robustness on the clean test set, while the ablation study should highlight the importance of the uncertainty-aware weights in mitigating the effects of label noise.

PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method for detecting label noise anomalies using variational autoencoders (VAEs). This method, LabelVAE, trains a VAE on the input data and learns a probabilistic representation of the clean data. By analyzing the distribution of latent variables, LabelVAE can identify instances that differ significantly from the clean data, indicating potential label noise.
CONTROLS: We compare LabelVAE against two strong baselines: 1) a standard VAE trained on the noisy data without anomaly detection and 2) a simple threshold-based approach that flags samples with high reconstruction error.

PREDICTION: LabelVAE should demonstrate high accuracy in detecting label noise anomalies, reducing the impact of label noise on downstream classification tasks.

TITLE: Combining Active Learning and Label Correction for Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: We propose a hybrid framework that combines active learning and label correction techniques to handle noisy labels. In this framework, we first use active learning to select the most informative samples, and then apply a label correction method (CorrEnsemble++) to refine the selected samples. This iterative process allows the model to adaptively learn from the most informative and reliable samples.
CONTROLS: We compare our framework against two baselines: 1) a traditional active learning approach without label correction and 2) a label correction method without active learning. We also include an ablation study to evaluate the effect of different active learning strategies.
COST: 92600
PREDICTION: Our proposed framework should achieve state-of-the-art results by effectively combining the strengths of active learning and label correction, leading to improved robustness and accuracy on clean test sets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Label Correction with Uncertainty-Aware Regularization
PROPOSAL: We provide a theoretical analysis of CorrEnsemble and its variants, focusing on the convergence properties of uncertainty-aware ensemble regularization in the presence of instance-dependent label noise. We establish bounds on the excess risk of CorrEnsemble and CorrEnsemble++ and explore the impact of different regularizers on the convergence rate.
CONTROLS: We compare our theoretical bounds against existing results for traditional active learning and differential privacy-based label correction methods.
COST: 100000
PREDICTION: Our theoretical analysis should provide insights into the effectiveness of uncertainty-aware ensemble regularization in handling instance-dependent label noise, shedding light on the origins of its robustness and potential limitations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Iterative Label Correction with Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Regularization
PROPOSAL: We design a method called "CorrEnsemble" that combines label correction and ensemble regularization techniques to iteratively refine the noisy labels. CorrEnsemble utilizes a novel variant of the state-of-the-art Mixup loss formulation that incorporates uncertainty-aware weights based on the predictions of a deep neural network ensemble. This allows the model to adaptively explore different label correction possibilities and learn from the long-term consequences of its decisions.
CONTROLS: We consider two strong baselines: 1) a standard neural network trained on the noisy labels without label correction and 2) an active learning-based approach that uses prediction loss and confidence levels to isolate and manage noisy labels. We also include an ablation study to evaluate the effect of the uncertainty-aware weights on the overall performance.
COST: 153000
PREDICTION: CorrEnsemble should show significant improvements over the baselines in terms of accuracy and robustness on the clean test set, while the ablation study should highlight the importance of the uncertainty-aware weights in mitigating the effects of label noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Instance-Dependent Label Noise on Deep Neural Network Generalization
PROPOSAL: We conduct an empirical study to investigate the effects of instance-dependent label noise on the generalization performance of deep neural networks. Using a dataset of images with synthetic instance-dependent label noise (such as MNIST or CIFAR-10), we compare the performance of different state-of-the-art deep learning models trained with noisy labels against their clean-label counterparts. Additionally, we analyze the effect of noise level, model architecture, and training epochs on the performance of these models.
CONTROLS: We consider six different models: ResNet, VGG16, DenseNet, Inception, AlexNet, and SqueezeNet, each trained with their respective clean and noisy label sets. We also include experiments with varying noise levels (5%, 10%, 20%) and training epoch budgets (50, 100, 150) to assess the robustness of each model in the presence of label noise.
COST: 126000
PREDICTION: This experiment should reveal the extent to which instance-dependent label noise affects the generalization performance of deep neural networks, highlighting the need for more robust methods to handle such noise.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Exploring Iterative Label Correction with Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Regularization (Rev)
PROPOSAL: We revise CorrEnsemble to incorporate transfer learning with pre-trained models, allowing it to leverage knowledge from robust models while adapting to the specific characteristics of the noisy dataset. By combining the uncertainty-aware ensemble regularization with transfer learning, CorrEnsemble becomes more robust and better able to handle instance-dependent label noise.
CONTROLS: We retain the strong baselines from the original proposal and include additional controls to evaluate the effect of transfer learning: 1) a pre-trained model without uncertainty-aware ensemble regularization and 2) the original CorrEnsemble method without transfer learning.
COST: 190500
PREDICTION: The revised CorrEnsemble should exhibit improved performance over the baselines, with significant gains in instance-dependent label noise scenarios, and the ablation study should demonstrate the synergy between transfer learning and uncertainty-aware ensemble regularization.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Exploring Iterative Label Correction with Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Regularization
PROPOSAL: We revise CorrEnsemble to incorporate a noise-aware sampling strategy that adaptively selects noisy samples based on their predicted uncertainty and correction potential. This revised method, CorrEnsemble+, should better identify the most problematic labels and focus the label correction efforts on these samples.
CONTROLS: We compare CorrEnsemble+ against the original CorrEnsemble and include an additional control to evaluate the effect of uncertainty-aware sampling: a baseline that uses traditional, fixed-value sampling.
COST: 184500
PREDICTION: CorrEnsemble+ should demonstrate improved robustness and accuracy compared to CorrEnsemble, especially in highly noisy scenarios, by more effectively targeting and correcting the most problematic labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Label Noise Anomaly Detection using Variational Autoencoders
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method for detecting label noise anomalies using variational autoencoders (VAEs). This method, LabelVAE, trains a VAE on the input data and learns a probabilistic representation of the clean data. By analyzing the distribution of latent variables, LabelVAE can identify instances that differ significantly from the clean data, indicating potential label noise.
CONTROLS: We compare LabelVAE against two strong baselines: 1) a standard VAE trained on the noisy data without anomaly detection and 2) a simple threshold-based approach that flags samples with high reconstruction error.
COST: 173200
PREDICTION: LabelVAE should demonstrate high accuracy in detecting label noise anomalies, reducing the impact of label noise on downstream classification tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Loss Functions for Instance-Dependent Label Noise
PROPOSAL: We design and evaluate a new family of robust loss functions that can adapt to instance-dependent label noise. These loss functions, inspired by game-theoretic and Bayesian risk models, assign lower weights to potentially noisy samples, making the model more robust to label noise.
CONTROLS: We compare our robust loss functions against traditional loss functions (e.g., cross-entropy loss) and recent robustness techniques (e.g., Mixup loss) that do not specifically address instance-dependent label noise.
COST: 212700
PREDICTION: Our proposed loss functions should significantly improve robustness to instance-dependent label noise compared to existing methods, demonstrating improved accuracy and stability on clean test sets.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Exploring Iterative Label Correction with Uncertainty-Aware Ensemble Regularization
PROPOSAL: We revisit CorrEnsemble and incorporate a global consistency check that measures the coherence of label corrections across different instances. This refinement, CorrEnsemble++, focuses on identifying and correcting local anomalies that might arise from naive ensemble regularization, further improving the robustness of label correction.
CONTROLS: We compare CorrEnsemble++ against the original CorrEnsemble, CorrEnsemble+, and the baseline without label correction. We also include a variant of CorrEnsemble++ that uses a different global consistency metric to assess the impact of different coherence measures.
COST: 231300
PREDICTION: CorrEnsemble++ should exhibit even higher accuracy and robustness than its predecessors, resulting from its ability to more effectively correct local anomalies and mitigate the effects of instance-dependent label noise.

TITLE:  Evaluating the Impact of Label Noise on Robust Loss Functions
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with a variety of existing robust loss functions, (Tversky loss, Focal loss, Mean Absolute Error, Cross-Entropy loss with MSE regularization), trained on the CIFAR-10 dataset and compared to standard cross-entropy loss on both clean and noisy labels. The noise will be introduced using the popular label corruption tool, implemented based on the protocol from the papers by Xiao et al., and Zakynthinou et al.

PREDICTION: We expect the robust loss functions to be able to significantly reduce the negative impact of label noise on the model's performance on clean test data, while the effect of the strongest robust loss function will be too narrow in terms of  model generalization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Noise-Robust Model Selection using Out-of-Distribution Label Detection
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection to identify and remove noisy instances during training. Specifically, we will train a discriminator to detect OOD labels, and select the data points that fall in the in-distribution region. This approach is tested on the noisy labels of the CIFAR-10 dataset and compared to existing label selection methods (e.g. Co-teaching). Furthermore, we introduce a noise detection module to the discriminator and evaluate the result on learning ability with noisy labels for CLIP model.
CONTROLS: Clipping the discriminator output (to see how pure OOD detection reduces selection accuracy), standard cross-entropy loss from turn 1, remove the detector from the model
COST: 600
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved robustness and accuracy of the model on OOD tasks using the OOD detection-based model selection approach, but detection might struggle with complex instance-dependent label distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semi-Supervised Learning with Uncertainty-Modulated Noisy Label Modeling
PROPOSAL: This experiment introduces uncertainty estimation on label noise patterns using a probabilistic label noise model. We employ a Bayesian neural network (BNN) that models the uncertainty of both data and noisy labels. This approach is tested on the noisy labels of the CIFAR-10 dataset. By selectively encouraging the neural network to learn from clean samples and reweighting noisy samples according to label uncertainty, the BNN is expected to outperform existing baseline methods like SCE (Self-ensembling methods) or Clean-Label. We also pair BNN with existing label selection methods and benchmark them on downstream tasks to see its limitations on learning ability.
CONTROLS: Fit a standard BNN on the dataset (without label uncertainty) to check baseline as below
COST: 936
PREDICTION: The experiment is expected to output higher improvements on CIFAR 10 test data, and yielding positive results with instance dependent noisy labels from individual features toward long term regime. But data imbalance remains a challenge in application scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Instance-dependent Label Error Correction with Meta-learning
PROPOSAL: This experiment introduces a meta-learning approach to correct instance-dependent label errors. We employ a meta-model that learns to specify corrections for individual instances based on their feature representations. The meta-model is trained on a set of examples with corresponding label corrections, and then used to correct labels in the target dataset. We will evaluate this approach on a variety of instance-dependent noisy label datasets, including synthetic and real-world datasets.
CONTROLS: Standard cross-entropy loss and a meta-learning baseline (without label corrections)
COST: 1870
PREDICTION: Expected improvements in model performance on target datasets due to the meta-learning approach, but potential challenges in handling large variations in label noise distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensemble Methods for Label Noise Correction through Model Aggregation
PROPOSAL: This experiment utilizes ensemble methods to correct label noise by aggregating predictions from multiple models, each trained on a different subset of the data. We will explore different ensemble methods, including bagging, boosting, and stacking, and evaluate their effectiveness in correcting label noise. We will also compare the performance of the ensemble methods to individual models trained on noisy labels.
CONTROLS: Standard cross-entropy loss and a selection of the previous methods (e.g. robust loss functions, semi-supervised learning)
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Expected improvements in model performance due to ensemble methods, particularly in cases with strong label noise, but potential challenges in balancing ensemble diversity and consistency.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Noisy Labels with Label-Noise-Aware Generators
PROPOSAL: This experiment introduces an adversarial training approach to correct noisy labels. We design a generator network that produces noisy labels, and a discriminator network that distinguishes between clean and noisy labels. The generator is trained to produce noisy labels that are indistinguishable from the true noisy labels, while the discriminator is trained to correctly classify the labels. We will evaluate this approach on a variety of noisy label datasets.
CONTROLS: Standard cross-entropy loss and a selection of the previous methods (e.g. robust loss functions, semi-supervised learning)
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Expected significant improvements in model performance due to the ability of the generator to accurately simulate noise in the data, but potential challenges in balancing generator and discriminator performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception from Low-Frame-Rate RGB Frames
PROPOSAL: We evaluate the performance of existing RGB-event fusion methods for multi-object segmentation at predicting a dense semantic map at an arbitrary timestamp within the perceptual gap between two consecutive low-frame-rate frames. We modify and train two of the most popular RGB-event fusion methods, MFFF (Learning to Fuse Multi-frame RGB and Event Data for Road Scene Understanding) and CET (Contextual Event-Triggered Attention for RGB-Event Fusion in Autonomous Driving Scenarios), on the KITTI-360 dataset and the NVIDIA DriveSim dataset, to analyze their performance in detecting and segmenting objects at varying offset times $\delta t \in (0, \Delta t]$. Specifically, we will test the performance of these methods on predicting vehicle and pedestrian detections at short, mid, and long offset times.
CONTROLS: We compare the results of the modified RGB-event fusion methods with several baselines: 1) using only the initial RGB frame $I_t$ for segmentation, 2) using only the event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$, and 3) multi-modal RGB-video fusion (RGB-Video Fusion Network for Autonomous Driving) that relies on dense RGB videos at high frame rates.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: We expect that while the RGB-event fusion methods would provide significant improvements over the baseline methods, their performance would degrade at longer offset times due to the spatial sparsity and high noise in the event stream, particularly in challenging autonomous driving scenarios where objects move, appear, or become occluded quickly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Event Context Aggregation
PROPOSAL: We propose a new hierarchical event context aggregation (HECA) method that leverages a spatial-temporal hierarchy to infer and aggregate event contexts within the perceptual gap. HECA starts by aggregating events across spatially adjacent regions, capturing local changes in brightness and object motion. It then hierarchically refines the aggregated events through multiple stages, fusing the spatial-temporal information and excluding outliers due to noisy event data. This results in a robust and rich event context representation, which we feed into a convolutional neural network (CNN) for dense semantic map inference at the target time. We train and evaluate HECA on the same datasets as the modified RGB-event fusion methods.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of HECA with the extended RGB-event fusion methods and the aforementioned baselines, focusing on scenes with dense and sparse event streams to analyze its robustness against varying event noise levels.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: We anticipate significant improvements in semantic segmentation accuracy at arbitrary offset times $\delta t \in (0, \Delta t]$ over the existing methods, particularly in scenes with rich and changing structures, due to the hierarchical event aggregation and the ability to exclude noise. However, its computational costs may be higher due to the aggregation process and hierarchical refinement stages.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Temporal Contextual Fusion
PROPOSAL: We suggest that the limitations of existing event-based fusion methods are due to their restrictive assumptions and force-fitting of the event stream into a fixed spatial context. To address this, we develop an adversarial temporal contextual fusion (ATCF) approach that allows for flexible temporal contextualization and adaptive aligning of event and RGB modalities. ATCF involves training a generative adversarial network (GAN) that optimizes for both the quality of the event-based contextual representation and the faithfulness of the spatial alignment between events and RGB frames. We then merge this learned contextual representation with a sequence-to-sequence model that outputs a segmented map at the target time. ATCF is trained and tested on challenging autonomous driving scenarios captured in the IROAD RADAR Sensor Platform series datasets.
CONTROLS: We evaluate ATCF against the existing event-based fusion methods and the aforementioned baselines, focusing on measuring its robustness and adaptability in scenes with varying dynamic contexts, speeds, and sensor challenges.
COST: 2200
PREDICTION: We predict that ATCF will provide state-of-the-art performance, robustness, and real-time processing capabilities for inferring high-quality, dense semantic maps at target times within perceptual gaps, outperforming existing RGB-event fusion approaches by enabling flexible temporal contextualization and selecting the most informative RGB event pairs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel temporal depth estimation (TDE) method to tackle the challenge of predicting depth maps at arbitrary timestamps within the perceptual gap. By leveraging the event stream and the initial RGB frame, TDE utilizes a convolutional neural network to learn a spatio-temporal depth representation of the scene, taking into account the object motion and layout. This depth map is then employed to enhance the segmentation model, providing additional contextual information about the scene geometry. TDE is designed to work in conjunction with the existing RGB-event fusion methods, such as the revised ATCF, and is evaluated on the IROAD RADAR Sensor Platform series datasets.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of TDE with the other proposed methods, focusing on measuring its ability to generate accurate depth maps and incorporate them into the segmentation process.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that TDE will improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation and object detection at arbitrary target times $\delta t \in (0, \Delta t]$, particularly in scenes with complex geometry and varying depth distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Occupancy Grid Mapping
PROPOSAL: To tackle the challenge of predicting dense semantic maps at arbitrary timestamps, we propose a robust occupancy grid mapping (ROGM) approach that utilizes the estimated depth maps from TDE and event data to construct an occupancy grid representation of the environment. By leveraging the advantageous features of combined event-video data, ROGM generates a robust mapping that accommodates complex geometries and dynamic scenes. We evaluate ROGM on challenging real-world datasets and its performance in enhancing semantic perception.
CONTROLS: We compare ROGM's performance with the combination of the revised ATCF and TDE on real-world datasets, such as the Waymo Open Dataset, using metrics that assess mapping accuracy and its impact on semantic perception.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: We predict that ROGM will provide robust and accurate mapping representation, leading to enhanced semantic perception at arbitrary target times, by leveraging the strengths of combined depth maps, event data, and occupancy grid formations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Learning for Event-Driven Perception
PROPOSAL: We propose an online learning framework for event-driven perception that enables the models to adapt to new environmental conditions and sensor noise over time. The framework incorporates an incremental learning module that fine-tunes the semantic segmentation network using event-based information and RGB frames encountered during actual deployment. By doing so, the model learns to rapport dynamic contexts and becomes more resilient to non-stationary events, such as changing lighting conditions or newly introduced obstacles. We implement this framework with TDE, ROGM, and ATCF models and evaluate its benefits in a drone navigation setting.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the online learning-based models with those trained in a batch setting, using metrics that assess adaptation rates and resilience to dynamic environments.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the online learning framework will enable the event-driven perception models to adapt and improve rapidly in real-world environments, leading to more accurate and robust predictions at arbitrary target times, particularly in scenarios with high variability in events and sensor data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decision Transformer for Event-Driven Perception
PROPOSAL: To tackle complex and dynamic events, such as multiple-agent interactions or challenging environmental conditions, we propose a novel Decision Transformer (DT) approach for event-driven perception. DT leverages a sequence-to-sequence framework that incorporates the TDE and ROGM models, enabling the network to predict semantic segmentation outputs at arbitrary target times based on the conditional probability of events up to a given timestamp. This approach allows for more accurate modeling of the event sequence and improves the overall perception performance in challenging and dynamic environments.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the DT model on a variety of datasets, including the provided dataset for drone navigation and the more challenging scenarios of pedestrian behavior and multi-agent interactions.
COST: 16000
PREDICTION: We expect the DT-based event-driven perception model to excel in predicting semantic outcomes in complex scenarios, showcasing a marked improvement in performance compared to existing approaches when handling challenging and dynamic events.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable and Interpretable Event-Driven Perception
PROPOSAL: To address the high computational costs of complex event-driven perception models, we propose a modular and interpretable architecture that incorporates feature reduction and attention mechanisms, allowing for faster prediction times without compromising performance. The Scalable and Interpretable Event-Driven Perception (SIEP) module is designed to learn informative features that are critical for accurate perception in real-time, making it well-suited for deployment on cost-sensitive robots and autonomous vehicles. We integrate SIEP with the existing proposals to evaluate its benefits on real-world benchmarks.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of SIEP-based models with their non-SIEP counterparts using metrics that assess prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and demands placed on computational resources, particularly for complex and high-speed environments.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: We predict that SIEP will enable real-time prediction of semantic segmentation outputs while providing explainable results for the decision-making process, ultimately leading to improved interpretability of the outputs and determination of real-time event-driven perception.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical RGB-Event Fusion Network
PROPOSAL: Introduce a Hierarchical RGB-Event Fusion Network (HREFN) that fuses static semantic context from RGB frames with temporally dense event streams. HREFN consists of a Convolutional Feature Pyramid Network (CFPN) that hierarchically extracts features from RGB frames, and a Temporal Feature Aggregation Network (TFAN) that aggregates and refines features from the event stream. The network takes the initial RGB frame $I_t$ and event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$ as input, and produces a dense semantic map for any $\delta t \in (0, \Delta t]$.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance with state-of-the-art RGB semantic segmentation methods (e.g., DeepLabv3+), as well as a fusion-based approach that only combines RGB features with event-counts.
COST: 1890
PREDICTION: HREFN should outperform the baselines, especially for longer prediction intervals and highly dynamic scenes, where the hierarchical feature extraction and temporal feature aggregation can effectively capture and propagate semantic context from the RGB frame to the event stream. However, the model may struggle with extreme occlusion scenarios where the event stream lacks sufficient information.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception using Event-Driven RGB Fusion
PROPOSAL: Develop a two-stage RGB-event fusion model, where the first stage uses a video segmentation model (e.g., I3D) to obtain an initial segmentation of the input frame $I_t$ based on the static semantic context. Then, in the second stage, an attention-based event processing module (e.g., Transformer) is used to fuse the initial segmentation with the temporally dense event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$. This attention mechanism selectively focuses on the most relevant past events, especially those corresponding to moving or dynamic objects, to generate accurate dense semantic predictions at any target time $t+\delta t$. Our model, dubbed "SEDGE" (SegmentationDriven Event-driven Dense GEneration), is designed to overcome the challenges of limited temporal context and noisy event data.
CONTROLS: I3D with pure RGB input, no-events baseline, videoransfer for segment consistency
COST: 160
PREDICTION: SEDGE achieves 5-7% improvement in semantic segmentation scores over the I3D baseline on real-world benchmarks for autonomous driving, drone navigation, and quadruped robot navigation.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Long-Term Event Memory for Causal High-Frame-Rate Perception
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel memory-augmented neural network module to leverage past events over a predefined long-term window, thereby maintaining a causal and anytime-capable perception framework. This module exploits the timeliness of events and efficiently retrieves relevant past events by employing a combination of temporal convolutional networks and densely connected memories. The memory is updated with a separate event processing component, eliminating the need for direct event-RGB fusion, which reduces computational overhead and alleviates potential noise accumulation issues.
CONTROLS: I3D with our SEDGE model without the long-term event memory, and a state-of-the-art video interpolation method
COST: 2880
PREDICTION: By using a long-term event memory with a window size of 10 frames (Δt=10), the model achieves 10% improvement in semantic segmentation scores with reduced error propagation, particularly for fast-moving objects in long-term prediction intervals.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Long-Term Event Memory for Causal High-Frame-Rate Perception
PROPOSAL: Modify the long-term event memory module to incorporate a temporal feature selection mechanism. This allows the model to selectively retain the most informative and temporally distant events, reducing the likelihood of negatively impacting prediction accuracy due to long-term event accumulation. Furthermore, we'll introduce a modulator for adaptively adjusting the memory's capacity and retention duration based on the scene dynamics andRGB perception. This adaptive nature will enable the model to dynamically balance between short-term and long-term predictive capabilities.

COST: 6480

TITLE: High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception using Event-Driven RGB Fusion
PROPOSAL: Develop a two-stage RGB-event fusion model, where the first stage uses a video segmentation model (e.g., I3D) to obtain an initial segmentation of the input frame $I_t$ based on the static semantic context. Then, in the second stage, an attention-based event processing module (e.g., Transformer) is used to fuse the initial segmentation with the temporally dense event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$. This attention mechanism selectively focuses on the most relevant past events, especially those corresponding to moving or dynamic objects, to generate accurate dense semantic predictions at any target time $t+\delta t$. Our model, dubbed "SEDGE" (SegmentationDriven Event-driven Dense GEneration), is designed to overcome the challenges of limited temporal context and noisy event data.
CONTROLS: I3D with pure RGB input, no-events baseline, videoransfer for segment consistency
COST: 480
PREDICTION: SEDGE achieves 5-7% improvement in semantic segmentation scores over the I3D baseline on real-world benchmarks for autonomous driving, drone navigation, and quadruped robot navigation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Long-Term Event Memory for Causal High-Frame-Rate Perception
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel memory-augmented neural network module to leverage past events over a predefined long-term window, thereby maintaining a causal and anytime-capable perception framework. This module exploits the timeliness of events and efficiently retrieves relevant past events by employing a combination of temporal convolutional networks and densely connected memories. The memory is updated with a separate event processing component, eliminating the need for direct event-RGB fusion, which reduces computational overhead and alleviates potential noise accumulation issues.
CONTROLS: I3D with our SEDGE model without the long-term event memory, and a state-of-the-art video interpolation method
COST: 8640
PREDICTION: By using a long-term event memory with a window size of 10 frames (Δt=10), the model achieves 10% improvement in semantic segmentation scores with reduced error propagation, particularly for fast-moving objects in long-term prediction intervals.

Furthermore, we'll introduce a modulator for adaptively adjusting the memory's capacity and retention duration based on the scene dynamics andRGB perception. This adaptive nature will enable the model to dynamically balance between short-term and long-term predictive capabilities.

COST: 19440
PREDICTION: By employing temporally adaptive long-term event caches, the revised model significantly reduces error amplification by up to 30% on maneuvers involving high speeds and occlusions, thus providing high-fidelity semantic predictions throughout the perception gap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dense Semantic Prediction with Causal RGB-Event Fusion
PROPOSAL: We propose a neural architecture that jointly processes the static RGB context and the temporal event stream, leveraging a sequence-to-sequence model to fuse information between frames. Specifically, we design a Causal Event-Conditioned RGB (eCRGB) network that learns to predict the future scene by conditioning on past events and using RGB features as an external trigger. The eCRGB network operates in a two-stage process: the first stage infers the conditional probability of the next events given the current RGB frame, and the second stage generates the future semantic map based on the predicted events and past RGB features.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method against multi-modal fusion techniques which rely only on RGB-D or RGB-event data, and also against a variant of our method with reversed causal orientation (i.e., future events used as input).
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our eCRGB method will substantially outperform state-of-the-art event-only semantic segmentation methods and competitive multi-modal fusion approaches in both accuracy and efficiency, while its causal nature enables anytime-prediction within the perceptual gap. However, it may fail to generalize to extremely long prediction intervals or highly dynamic scenes without sufficient temporal context.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RGB-Event Hybrid Training
PROPOSAL: To leverage the strengths of both RGB and event cameras while addressing their respective weaknesses, we propose a RGB-Event Hybrid Training (REHT) framework. REHT aims to encode the RGB-based understanding of static semantic context and complement it with fine-grained temporal information captured by the event stream. We will train the model using a combination of RGB and event data in an alternating manner: for each mini-batch, the model receives either RGB-D or RGB-event pairs. This deterministic process is analogous to switch between traversing only one branch of a Feynman diagram in physics, while nonetheless benefiting from both the pixel-level and event-level branches collectively. This ensures our model selectively integrates disparate modalities, efficiently encoding their outputs into a highly effective, final representation that consistently boosts accuracy and efficiency.
CONTROLS: To compare REHT against conventional multi-modal fusion techniques, we will also train a model that is trained entirely with RGB-D data as well as another model with RGB-event data, which serves as the baseline.
COST: 240 GPU-hours
PREDICATION: REHT will improve dense semantic prediction of eCRGB significantly and adapt to big variations in their inputs, thereby easily maintaining a balance between theoretical accuracy, usability, and (qualitatively marginalized) computing overhead; however, failure may arise if relying on different relative dataset sizes that would otherwise significantly affect long-term training efficacy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Attention Mechanism for eCRGB
PROPOSAL: To directly address the spatial sparsity of event data and better contextualize relevant events within the RGB frame, we incorporate a Temporal Attention Mechanism (TAM) into the eCRGB network. The TAM module learns to dynamically weigh the importance of events across time, creating a compact and cohesive representation of the event sequence. By selectively focusing on the most relevant events, our model can more accurately reason about the scene's evolution and make informed predictions about the future.
CONTROLS: We will compare the tam-enhanced eCRGB against the original eCRGB and compare the attention weights learned during training to better understand the model's decision-making process.
COST: 540 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The incorporation of TAM is expected to improve the model's ability to handle sparse event data and promote more accurate predictions in high-dynamic-range scenarios. However, it may introduce additional computational overhead and require careful tuning of hyperparameters to avoid performance degradation.

TITLE: Using Optical Flow for Event Camera Data Augmentation
PROPOSAL: To adapt the eCRGB network to handle event data with varying densities without overfitting, we will incorporate optical flow-based data augmentation in the training process. By simulating the effect of different optical flow fields on the event sequence, we can artificially create new scenarios with varying levels of event density, effectively increasing the model's robustness and adaptability to unpredictable environments. This approach is tailored to address the sparse and irregular nature of event data, allowing the eCRGB network to generalize better to real-world scenarios.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the effectiveness of optical flow-based data augmentation by comparing the model's performance on real-world event data with and without this technique.
COST: 1080 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The incorporation of optical flow-based data augmentation is expected to improve the eCRGB network's robustness and ability to adapt to diverse event densities, leading to more accurate and reliable predictions in real-world scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning from RGB Domains to Event Cameras
PROPOSAL: To alleviate the scarcity of event camera datasets and accelerate the development of event-based computer vision models, we propose a transfer learning approach that Repurposes pre-trained RGB-based models and fine-tunes them for event cameras. By leveraging the rich literature on RGB-based models, we can adapt existing architectures to the unique characteristics of event cameras, such as their asynchronous and event-based nature. This approach can significantly reduce the time and computational resources required to develop and train event-based models.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the effectiveness of transfer learning by comparing the performance of event-based models trained from scratch against those fine-tuned from pre-trained RGB-based models.
COST: 2400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The transfer learning approach is expected to significantly accelerate the development of event-based computer vision models, leading to faster progress in the field. However, the success of this approach depends on the quality of the pre-trained models and the fine-tuning process, which requires careful hyperparameter tuning and selection.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dense Semantic Prediction with Causal RGB-Event Fusion
PROPOSAL: We propose a neural architecture that jointly processes the static RGB context and the temporal event stream, leveraging a sequence-to-sequence model to fuse information between frames. Specifically, we design a Causal Event-Conditioned RGB (eCRGB) network that learns to predict the future scene by conditioning on past events and using RGB features as an external trigger. The eCRGB network operates in a two-stage process: the first stage infers the conditional probability of the next events given the current RGB frame, and the second stage generates the future semantic map based on the predicted events and past RGB features.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method against multi-modal fusion techniques which rely only on RGB-D or RGB-event data, and also against a variant of our method with reversed causal orientation (i.e., future events used as input).
COST: 450 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our eCRGB method will substantially outperform state-of-the-art event-only semantic segmentation methods and competitive multi-modal fusion approaches in both accuracy and efficiency, while its causal nature enables anytime-prediction within the perceptual gap. However, it may fail to generalize to extremely long prediction intervals or highly dynamic scenes without sufficient temporal context.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RGB-Event Hybrid Training
PROPOSAL: To leverage the strengths of both RGB and event cameras while addressing their respective weaknesses, we propose a RGB-Event Hybrid Training (REHT) framework. REHT aims to encode the RGB-based understanding of static semantic context and complement it with fine-grained temporal information captured by the event stream. We will train the model using a combination of RGB and event data in an alternating manner: for each mini-batch, the model receives either RGB-D or RGB-event pairs. This deterministic process is analogous to switch between traversing only one branch of a Feynman diagram in physics, while nonetheless benefiting from both the pixel-level and event-level branches collectively. This ensures our model selectively integrates disparate modalities, efficiently encoding their outputs into a highly effective, final representation that consistently boosts accuracy and efficiency.
CONTROLS: To compare REHT against conventional multi-modal fusion techniques, we will also train a model that is trained entirely with RGB-D data as well as another model with RGB-event data, which serves as the baseline.
COST: 720 GPU-hours
PREDICATION: REHT will improve dense semantic prediction of eCRGB significantly and adapt to big variations in their inputs, thereby easily maintaining a balance between theoretical accuracy, usability, and (qualitatively marginalized) computing overhead; however, failure may arise if relying on different relative dataset sizes that would otherwise significantly affect long-term training efficacy.

PROPOSAL: To improve the eCRGB's sequential processing capability and enhance its ability to capture nuanced temporal relationships, we will redesign the first stage of the eCRGB network to adopt a recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture, specifically a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), to infer the conditional probability of the next events given the current RGB frame. This will allow the model to preserve information over time and adapt to changing scene dynamics more effectively. By using GRU instead of the original feed-forward layers, we can harness the power of sequential modeling and encode richer temporal context into our predictions.

The TAM module learns to dynamically weigh the importance of events across time, creating a compact and cohesive representation of the event sequence. By selectively focusing on the most relevant events, our model can more accurately reason about the scene's evolution and make informed predictions about the future.

PROPOSAL: To adapt the eCRGB network to handle event data with varying densities without overfitting, we will incorporate optical flow-based data augmentation in the training process. By simulating the effect of different optical flow fields on the event sequence, we can artificially create new scenarios with varying levels of event density, effectively increasing the model's robustness and adaptability to unpredictable environments. This approach is tailored to address the sparse and irregular nature of event data, allowing the eCRGB network to generalize better to real-world scenarios.

PROPOSAL: To alleviate the scarcity of event camera datasets and accelerate the development of event-based computer vision models, we propose a transfer learning approach that Repurposes pre-trained RGB-based models and fine-tunes them for event cameras. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalized 3D Generation via Image-to-3D Diffusion
PROPOSAL: Train a text-to-image diffusion model (e.g. DALL-E) on a dataset of images and their corresponding 3D models. Finetune this model on a small set of images of a specific subject, by adding a few subject-specific tokens to the input text. Use the resulting model to generate 3D models from novel viewpoints, by inputting a text prompt that guides the generation towards a specific view. Evaluate the generated 3D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.
CONTROLS: Baselines include state-of-the-art 3D generation models, ablations include models trained without subject-specific tokens or finetuning, and controls include evaluation on a set of real-world images and 3D models.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The personalized model will outperform the baselines on accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance, but may suffer from overfitting to the few subject-specific images used during finetuning. This approach may fail for subjects with complex or varying appearances.

TITLE: Subject-Aware 3D Generation via Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Train a 3D generation model on a dataset of images and their corresponding 3D models, while incorporating a contrastive learning objective that encourages the model to distinguish between different subjects. This can be achieved using a Siamese network architecture, where one branch of the network is used to generate a 3D model from a given image, and the other branch is used to generate a negative example that is similar to the first but belongs to a different subject. Evaluate the generated 3D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.

PREDICTION: The contrastive learning approach will improve the accuracy of shape and texture, and reduce the negative transfer issue, but may require a large dataset of diverse subjects to train the model effectively.

PROPOSAL: Train a text-to-2D image model on a large dataset of images of various subjects. Finetune this model on a small set of images of a specific subject, similar to the previous proposal. Then, use this subject-specific 2D model to guide a 3D generation model, such as a 3D diffusion model, to generate 3D models. Evaluate the generated 3D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.
CONTROLS: The 2D model is finetuned without subject-specific tokens, and the 3D diffusion model is used without guidance from the 2D model, to serve as additional baselines.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: The transfer learning approach will improve the accuracy of shape and texture, but may suffer from negative transfer if the 2D model is not well-aligned with the 3D domain. This approach may fail if the subject-specific 2D model does not capture the essential features of the subject's appearance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED - Transfer Learning from Subject-Driven 2D Generation to 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Similar to the previous proposal, train a text-to-2D image model on a large dataset of images of various subjects. However, instead of finetuning the 2D model on a small set of images of a specific subject, use multiple 2D images of the subject, taken from different viewpoints, to provide additional guidance to the 3D generation model. This can be achieved by creating a multi-modal input for the 3D model, which includes both the text prompt and the 2D images.
CONTROLS: The 2D model is used without subject-specific tokens, and the 3D model is used without guidance from the 2D images, to serve as additional baselines.
COST: 5040
PREDICTION: The multi-modal approach will improve the accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance, and reduce the negative transfer issue, but may increase the complexity of the model and require more data to train.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED - Transfer Learning from Subject-Driven 2D Generation to 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Similar to the previous proposal, train a text-to-2D image model on a large dataset of images of various subjects. However, instead of using multiple 2D images of the subject, taken from different viewpoints, to provide additional guidance to the 3D generation model, use a few 2D images of the subject, taken from novel viewpoints (e.g. side or back views), to help the 3D model learn to hallucinate those viewpoints more accurately. This can be achieved by adding a few 2D images to the input of the 3D model, and using them to refine the generation process.
CONTROLS: The 2D model is finetuned without subject-specific tokens, and the 3D model is used without guidance from the 2D images, to serve as additional baselines.
COST: 5280
PREDICTION: The use of 2D images from novel viewpoints will improve the accuracy of hallucinated viewpoints, but may require more data and computational resources to train the model effectively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Subject-Aware 3D Generation via Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Train a 3D generation model on a dataset of images and their corresponding 3D models, while incorporating a contrastive learning objective that encourages the model to distinguish between different subjects. This can be achieved using a Siamese network architecture, where one branch of the network is used to generate a 3D model from a given image, and the other branch is used to generate a negative example that is similar to the first but belongs to a different subject. Evaluate the generated 3D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.
CONTROLS: Baselines include state-of-the-art 3D generation models, ablations include models that do not use contrastive learning, and controls include evaluation on a set of real-world images and 3D models.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: The contrastive learning approach will improve the accuracy of shape and texture, and reduce the negative transfer issue, but may require a large dataset of diverse subjects to train the model effectively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Video-to-4D Generation with Subject-Preserving Constraints
PROPOSAL: Train a 4D generation model on a dataset of videos and their corresponding 4D models, while incorporating subject-preserving constraints that encourage the model to maintain the identity of the subject across different viewpoints and time steps. This can be achieved using a consistency loss function that measures the similarity between the generated 4D model and the input video, as well as the similarity between different views of the generated 4D model. Evaluate the generated 4D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.
CONTROLS: Baselines include state-of-the-art 4D generation models, ablations include models that do not use subject-preserving constraints, and controls include evaluation on a set of real-world videos and 4D models.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: The subject-preserving constraints will improve the accuracy of shape and texture, and reduce the negative transfer issue, but may require a large dataset of diverse subjects to train the model effectively, and may slow down the training process due to the additional computational cost of the consistency loss function.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED - Transfer Learning from Subject-Driven 2D Generation to 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Modify the previous proposal by using a few 3D models of the subject, taken from different viewpoints, in addition to the 2D images, to provide more guidance to the 3D generation model. This can be achieved by creating a multi-modal input for the 3D model, which includes both the text prompt, the 2D images, and the 3D models. Evaluate the generated 3D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.
CONTROLS: The 2D model is finetuned without subject-specific tokens, and the 3D model is used without guidance from the 2D images, to serve as additional baselines.
COST: 5040
PREDICTION: The multi-modal input will improve the accuracy of shape and texture, and reduce the negative transfer issue, by providing more information about the subject's appearance from different viewpoints. However, this may increase the complexity of the model and require more data to train effectively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical 3D Generation with Subject-Specific Refinement
PROPOSAL: Train a hierarchical 3D generation model that first generates a coarse 3D model from an input image, and then refines this model using a subject-specific 3D model that has been pre-trained on a dataset of images and 3D models of the subject. This can be achieved using a two-stage training process, where the coarse model is trained first, and then the refinement model is trained to refine the output of the coarse model. Evaluate the generated 3D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.
CONTROLS: Baselines include state-of-the-art 3D generation models, ablations include models that do not use hierarchical generation or subject-specific refinement, and controls include evaluation on a set of real-world images and 3D models.
COST: 7560
PREDICTION: The hierarchical generation and subject-specific refinement will improve the accuracy of shape and texture, and reduce the negative transfer issue, by allowing the model to focus on refining the most important aspects of the subject's appearance. However, this may increase the complexity of the model and require more data to train effectively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generative Adversarial Networks for Subject-Aware 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Train a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) that consists of a generator network that generates 3D models from input images, and a discriminator network that evaluates the generated 3D models and provides feedback to the generator network. The generator network is trained to produce 3D models that are consistent with the input image and conform to the subject's appearance, while the discriminator network is trained to distinguish between real and fake 3D models. Evaluate the generated 3D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.
CONTROLS: Baselines include state-of-the-art 3D generation models, ablations include models that do not use GANs, and controls include evaluation on a set of real-world images and 3D models.
COST: 10560
PREDICTION: The GAN-based approach will improve the accuracy of shape and texture, and reduce the negative transfer issue, by allowing the model to learn from both real and fake data. However, this may require more computational resources and data to train effectively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exemplar-Based 3D Generation for Emphasized Subject Attributes
PROPOSAL: Train a 3D generation model that takes as input a set of exemplar 3D models that emphasize specific attributes of the subject, such as facial expressions or body poses. The model learns to generate 3D models that are similar to these exemplars, while also preserving the overall appearance and shape of the subject. This can be achieved by using an exemplar-based loss function that encourages the generated model to be similar to the exemplars. Evaluate the generated 3D models using metrics such as accuracy of shape, texture, and appearance.
CONTROLS: Baselines include state-of-the-art 3D generation models, ablations include models that do not use exemplars, and controls include evaluation on a set of real-world images and 3D models.
COST: 12960
PREDICTION: The exemplar-based approach will improve the accuracy of shape and texture, and allow for more control over the generated attributes, while also increasing the complexity of the model and requiring more data to train effectively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalized 3D Generation with Subject-Prior Score Matching
PROPOSAL: Train a state-of-the-art 3D generative model (e.g., DeepSDF) and enforce a subject-specific prior by adding a term to the loss function that maximizes the similarity between the generated 3D asset and a 2D diffusion prior learned from a few images of the target subject. This 2D diffusion prior serves as an indirect representation of the underlying appearance and structure of the subject.
CONTROLS: Baseline: a standard 3D generative model without the subject-prior loss term. Ablation study: removing the subject-prior term.
COST: 42
PREDICTION: The proposed method will achieve better semantic identity preservation than the standard 3D generative model, particularly in views not seen during training. It may, however, suffer from reduced quality or over-smoothing of textures due to the averaging effect of the 2D diffusion prior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Subject-Prior Learning with Unseen View Synthesis
PROPOSAL: Integrating the proposed subject-prior score matching method (Proposal 1) with a view synthesis technique (e.g., Plenoxels) to generate synthetic views of the subject from the 2D images used to train the diffusion prior. This will provide the model with more robust and diverse cues about the subject's appearance, thereby enhancing identity preservation for unseen views.
CONTROLS: Baselines: the original subject-prior score matching method (Proposal 1) and a view synthesis-only approach using the same view synthesis technique. Ablation study: replacing the diffusion prior with a learned view representation.
COST: 118.88
PREDICTION: The combined approach will lead to significantly improved semantic identity preservation, especially for novel views. However, it may introduce additional computational costs and potentially increase overfitting if the view synthesis component is not carefully regularized.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Enhancing Subject-Prior Learning with Unseen View Synthesis
PROPOSAL: Modify the previous proposal to instead generate spherical harmonics (SH) coefficients from the 2D images, which are then used as a representation of the subject's appearance in various views. This SH-based representation can be incorporated into the 3D generative model as an additional latent code. We hypothesize that this representation can better capture the spatial correlations between views, resulting in improved identity preservation.
CONTROLS: Baselines: the previous view synthesis approach and a baseline method using only SH coefficients without the 3D generative model.
COST: 163.5
PREDICTION: The revised method should exhibit better performance in preserving semantic identity across views, but may require further optimization to effectively integrate the SH coefficients with the 3D generative model.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity-Aware 3D Generative Model with Adversarial Loss
PROPOSAL: Modify the original 3D generative model (e.g., DeepSDF) by incorporating an identity-aware adversarial loss that encourages the model to produce 3D assets with a unique appearance and structure, distinct from other subjects in the training set. This can be achieved by training a discriminator that distinguishes between 3D assets of different subjects and providing a penalty signal to the generator when its output is indistinguishable from the rest.
CONTROLS: Baseline: a standard 3D generative model without the identity-aware adversarial loss. Ablation study: using a per-subject classification head to determine whether the generated asset belongs to the target subject.
COST: 151.2
PREDICTION: The proposed method should help improve semantic identity preservation by forcing the model to be more discriminative about the subject's appearance. However, it may increase mode collapse and require careful tuning of hyperparameters to manage the trade-off between identity preservation and overall quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multiresolution Conditional Diffusion for Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Integrate a multiresolution conditional diffusion model (e.g., WaveletDiffusion) that refines the output of a low-resolution 3D generative model (e.g., DeepSDF) to produce high-fidelity, personalized 3D assets. The model will learn to capture both global structure and local details, leading to improved semantic identity preservation and texture accuracy.
CONTROLS: Baselines: the low-resolution 3D generative model and the high-resolution diffusion model alone. Ablation study: using a different conditioning mechanism (e.g., label-based vs. image-based conditioning).
COST: 227.352
PREDICTION: The proposed method should yield state-of-the-art results in personalized 3D generation, particularly in terms of texture accuracy and global structure preservation. However, it may require a considerable amount of training data and computational resources, and potential overfitting issues need to be carefully handled.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Identity-Aware 3D Generative Model with Adversarial Loss
PROPOSAL: Refine the previous identity-aware adversarial loss by incorporating a multi-scale feature extraction mechanism that leverages both low-level texture features and high-level structural information. This can be achieved by concatenating or conditioning the discriminator's intermediate features with the generated asset's 3D spatial coordinates. This modified loss function should further improve semantic identity preservation by being more sensitive to both global and local variations.
CONTROLS: Baselines: the original identity-aware adversarial loss and a variant that only conditions the low-level features. Ablation study: using a stronger discriminator losses or a different conditioning mechanism (e.g., spherical harmonics coefficients).
COST: 280
PREDICTION: The revised method should demonstrate improved performance in capturing the subject's unique features across different scales and aspects, potentially leading to higher semantic identity preservation and better-quality 3D assets. However, it may increase computational requirements and training times, requiring careful balancing of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Cycle Consistency Loss for Personalized 4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop a hierarchical cycle consistency loss function to capture the temporal evolution of personalized 4D assets (animated 3D models). This loss will ensure that the model generates consistent and identity-preserving animations across different time steps, while also capturing the subtle variations in the subject's appearance and motion over time.
CONTROLS: Baselines: a standard cycle consistency loss and a variant that only considers low-resolution 4D assets. Ablation study: using different levels of hierarchical consistency (e.g., frame-wise vs. segment-wise).

However, it may introduce additional computational and memory requirements, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters to balance consistency and quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Makeup Transfer with Personalized 3D Rendering for Identity Preservation
PROPOSAL: Develop a new application of the proposed personalized 3D generation methods: transferring makeup or other cosmetic features from a reference image to a generated 3D asset of a subject. This can be achieved by incorporating a separate makeup transfer network that takes the reference image and the generated 3D asset as input, while leveraging the subject's identity features learned from the earlier methods to ensure accurate and personalized transfer.
CONTROLS: Baselines: state-of-the-art makeup transfer methods that do not leverage personalized 3D generation, as well as a variant that only uses the proposed subject-prior score matching method. Evaluation metrics: both subjective (user study) and objective (scarab metrics, FID score).
COST: 468
PREDICTION: The proposed makeup transfer method should enable accurate and personalized transfer of cosmetic features between subjects, with the potential to revolutionize applications in entertainment, fashion, and healthcare. However, it may require further refinement to handle challenging cases such as complex makeup designs, insufficient training data, or varying lighting conditions.

CONTROLS: Baselines: the original identity-aware adversarial loss and a variant that only conditions the low-level features. Ablation study: using a stronger discriminator losses or a different conditioning mechanism (e.g., spherical harmonics coefficients).
COST: 843
PREDICTION: The revised method should demonstrate improved performance in capturing the subject's unique features across different scales and aspects, potentially leading to higher semantic identity preservation and better-quality 3D assets. However, it may increase computational requirements and training times, requiring careful balancing of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Cycle Consistency Loss for Personalized 4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop a hierarchical cycle consistency loss function to capture the temporal evolution of personalized 4D assets (animated 3D models). This loss will ensure that the model generates consistent and identity-preserving animations across different time steps, while also capturing the subtle variations in the subject's appearance and motion over time.
CONTROLS: Baselines: a standard cycle consistency loss and a variant that only considers low-resolution 4D assets. Ablation study: using different levels of hierarchical consistency (e.g., frame-wise vs. segment-wise).
COST: 971
PREDICTION: The proposed hierarchical cycle consistency loss should enable the model to accurately capture the subject's personalized characteristics, motion, and temporal evolution, potentially leading to more realistic and engaging 4D assets. However, it may introduce additional computational and memory requirements, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters to balance consistency and quality.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Hierarchical Cycle Consistency Loss for Personalized 4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Refine the previous hierarchical cycle consistency loss by incorporating a conditional variant that takes into account the subject's identity features and the input video frames during the temporal inference process. This conditional loss should enable the model to generate more personalized and coherent animations that are adapted to the subject's unique characteristics and motion patterns.
CONTROLS: Baselines: the original hierarchical cycle consistency loss and a variant that removes the conditional component. Ablation study: using different types of conditional inputs (e.g., identity features, pose estimates, etc.).
COST: 1221
PREDICTION: The revised conditional hierarchical cycle consistency loss should demonstrate significant improvements in generating personalized and coherent 4D assets, while also reducing the likelihood of mode collapse and other quality issues. However, it may introduce additional computational and memory requirements, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters to balance quality and efficiency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Makeup Transfer with Personalized 3D Rendering for Identity Preservation
PROPOSAL: Develop a new application of the proposed personalized 3D generation methods: transferring makeup or other cosmetic features from a reference image to a generated 3D asset of a subject. This can be achieved by incorporating a separate makeup transfer network that takes the reference image and the generated 3D asset as input, while leveraging the subject's identity features learned from the earlier methods to ensure accurate and personalized transfer.
CONTROLS: Baselines: state-of-the-art makeup transfer methods that do not leverage personalized 3D generation, as well as a variant that only uses the proposed subject-prior score matching method. Evaluation metrics: both subjective (user study) and objective (scarab metrics, FID score).
COST: 1397
PREDICTION: The proposed makeup transfer method should enable accurate and personalized transfer of cosmetic features between subjects, with the potential to revolutionize applications in entertainment, fashion, and healthcare. However, it may require further refinement to handle challenging cases such as complex makeup designs, insufficient training data, or varying lighting conditions.

ACTION: REVISE 6
TITLE: Makeup Transfer with Personalized 3D Rendering for Identity Preservation
PROPOSAL: Refine the previous makeup transfer method by leveraging the insights and components from the other proposed methods (e.g., subject-prior score matching, hierarchical cycle consistency loss). This can be achieved by incorporating a hierarchical 3D-CVAE architecture that takes into account the subject's identity features, the makeup transfer network, and the personalization techniques from the earlier methods, to generate more realistic, personalized, and coherent 3D assets.
CONTROLS: Baselines: the original makeup transfer method, a variant that incorporates only the subject-prior score matching method, and a state-of-the-art method without personalized 3D generation. Evaluation metrics: both subjective (user study) and objective (scarab metrics, FID score).
COST: 1659
PREDICTION: The revised makeup transfer method should lead to more accurate and personalized transfer of cosmetic features between subjects, with significant improvements in realism and coherence of the generated 3D assets. However, it may require significant computational resources and careful tuning of hyperparameters to balance quality and efficiency.

TITLE: Identity-Preserving 3D Generation via Multi-View Pre-Training
PROPOSAL: We pre-train a 3D generator on a synthetic dataset of 3D objects with multiple views, optimizing for identity preservation by matching the object's appearance across different viewpoints. COST: 16,700
PREDICTION: We expect improved identity preservation, but may face challenges in disentangling viewpoint-invariant and viewpoint-dependent features.

TITLE: Personalized 3D Asset Generation via Diffusion-based Identity Fusion
PROPOSAL: Train a 3D diffusion model on a large synthetic dataset of objects with diverse appearances, and then fine-tune it using a small number of example images of the specific subject. Introduce an identity fusion mechanism to combine the learned 3D shape and appearance, and adapt the 3D model's diffusion process to preserve the subject's identity across viewpoints.

PREDICTION: The proposed approach successfully preserves the identity of the subject, achieving improved accuracy and personalization in 3D asset generation, but may struggle with cases where the input images have significant pose or viewpoint variations, or when the subject's appearance is highly distinct from the training dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparative Study of Image-to-3D and Video-to-4D Generation for Personalization
PROPOSAL: Evaluate and compare the performance of state-of-the-art 3D and 4D generative models, trained on synthetic datasets, in achieving personalization for a range of subjects and viewpoints. Assess the robustness of each generation approach to variations in input data, output views, and the realism of generated content.
CONTROLS: Baseline: publicly available 3D and 4D generation models; Ablation: compare performance with/without input data augmentation (image/video noise, blur, etc.).
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The comparison highlights the strengths and limitations of image-to-3D and video-to-4D generation, showing that video data often leads to more consistent appearance and motion across viewpoints, but can be sensitive to pose and viewpoint changes in the input video, while 3D generation tends to be more robust but suffers from upper-body imagery hallucinations.

TITLE: Investigating the Role of Multi-View Consistency in Personalized 3D and 4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Design and conduct an experimental study to investigate the effect of multi-view consistency on personalized 3D and 4D generation, using a range of metrics and evaluation protocols to assess the impact of consistency on generated assets. This will provide insights into the importance of consistency in achieving realistic and personalized results.
CONTROLS: Baseline: publicly available 3D and 4D generation models; Ablations: compare performance with different levels of multi-view consistency (e.g., loose, tight, no consistency).
COST: 16700
PREDICTION: The study highlights the critical role of multi-view consistency in achieving high-quality personalized 3D and 4D generation, but also reveals that excessive emphasis on consistency can lead to over-smoothing and loss of detail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring the Application of Personalized 3D and 4D Generation to Real-World Use Cases
PROPOSAL: Conduct a feasibility study to investigate the application of personalized 3D and 4D generation to real-world use cases, such as augmented reality, virtual try-on, and 3D printing. This will involve adapting existing models for these use cases and evaluating their performance in real-world scenarios.
CONTROLS: Baseline: publicly available 3D and 4D generation models; Ablations: compare performance with adapted models for specific use cases.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: The study demonstrates the potential for personalized 3D and 4D generation to have a significant impact on real-world applications, but also reveals challenges related to data availability, model adaptation, and evaluation metrics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Comparative Analysis of Personalized 3D and 4D Generation Models using Diverse Evaluation Metrics
PROPOSAL: Conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed personalized 3D and 4D generation models using a diverse set of evaluation metrics, including perceptual similarity, feature similarity, user studies, and quantitative metrics (e.g., PSNR, SSIM). This will provide a thorough understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of each model and help identify areas for future improvement.
CONTROLS: Baseline: publicly available 3D and 4D generation models; Ablations: compare performance with different evaluation metrics and model variants.
COST: 26750
PREDICTION: The comparative analysis reveals that each model excels in different aspects, but also highlights opportunities for further improvement, such as incorporating human evaluation and937 adaptive perplexity metrics that more accurately reflect user preferences.
