textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Deep Freeze Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers: Identifying Optimal Initial Scales for Post-Training Quantization
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of quantizing high-variance activation statistics associated with data-independent special tokens, we will propose a novel approach called Deep Freeze Quantization (DFQ). DFQ introduces an initial scale factor for each layer and token type, frozen during PTQ and pre-learned from a small set of representative calibration samples. We will investigate various initial scale learning schemes, including least-squares regression, adaptive learning rates, and manually-defined scales based on network architectures.
CONTROLS: We will compare DFQ with different initial scale learning schemes to techniques such as data-dependent quantization and compare its impact on VGGT's accuracy after PTQ on ScanNet.
COST: 4032
PREDICTION: We expect DFQ to improve the robustness and accuracy of PTQ for VGGT in 3D reconstruction tasks, especially when dealing with special tokens. However, empirically selecting the best initial scale factor may be challenging due to the high dimensionality of the search space.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Yield Similarity-Based Calibration Set Construction for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel calibration set construction method based on cross-yield similarity among scenes reconstructed by VGGT. This approach computes similarity measures between yields produced by VGGT on pairs of scenes and selects calibration samples from diverse yield clusters. We will evaluate the performance of this approach on ScanNet and compare it with the baseline calibration set construction methods.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the cross-yield similarity-based calibration set construction with the baseline calibration set construction methods and investigate the effect of varying yield similarity thresholds on the quality of the constructed calibration set.
COST: 3601.4
PREDICTION: We expect the cross-yield similarity-based calibration set construction to achieve better performance in terms of generalization to unseen scenes and robustness to outlier samples, by capturing scene yield patterns that are representative of real-world scenarios. However, the choice of yield similarity threshold may be challenging due to its sensitivity to specific scene and VGGT configurations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Training for Deep Freeze Quantization (DFQ-QAT)
PROPOSAL: We propose to extend the Deep Freeze Quantization (DFQ) approach by incorporating quantization-aware training (QAT) during the fine-tuning phase of PTQ. Specifically, we will use simulated quantization noise to train DFQ, allowing it to learn robust representations that are invariant to the noise and can better capture the underlying patterns in the data.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of DFQ-QAT with the baseline DFQ and data-dependent quantization techniques on ScanNet and evaluate its impact on VGGT's accuracy after PTQ.
COST: 8640
PREDICTION: We expect the quantization-aware training of DFQ (DFQ-QAT) to improve the accuracy and robustness of PTQ for VGGT in 3D reconstruction tasks by learning representations that can better handle quantization noise. However, the added computational cost of QAT may be significant, and its effect on the calibration complexity needs to be carefully evaluated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analytical and Empirical Risk Bounds for Post-Training Quantization of 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: We will derive analytical risk bounds for post-training quantization of 3D reconstruction transformers, based on the maximum likelihood estimation of the quantization ranges. We will also provide empirical risk bounds through extensive finite-sample simulations on ScanNet, evaluating the performance of various quantization techniques and providing a comprehensive assessment of their statistical efficiency.
CONTROLS: We will compare the analytical and empirical risk bounds with existing results for 2D vision tasks and language models, and investigate the trade-offs between calibration complexity, quantization accuracy, and model performance.
COST: 12960
PREDICTION: We expect the analytical and empirical risk bounds to provide valuable insights into the design of efficient and accurate post-training quantization schemes for 3D reconstruction transformers, while highlighting potential challenges and limitations of current approaches.

TITLE: Efficient Hardware Acceleration for Post-Training Quantization of 3D Reconstruction Transformers

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Calibration Set Size and Diversity Effects on Post-Training Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: We will train and evaluate the VGGT model with PTQ on the ScanNet dataset, while carefully controlling the diversity of the calibration set through data curation and normalization by representatives (i.e., using a varying number of diverse, representative scenes and balancing their sizes within each calibration set). We will vary the calibration set size from 100 to 1000 samples to examine the trade-off between accuracy and calibration complexity.
CONTROLS: We will include baseline PTQ experiments using a fixed calibration set size and evaluate performance under both calibrated and non-calibrated PTQ settings.
COST: 4872
PREDICTION: We expect improvements in calibration robustness with larger calibration set sizes, but a point of diminishing returns beyond 500-1000 calibration samples, where further increases begin to plateau. Potential failure lies in empirical variations in dataset sampling and representative definition.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Deep Freeze Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers: Identifying Optimal Initial Scales for Post-Training Quantization
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of quantizing high-variance activation statistics associated with data-independent special tokens, we will propose a novel approach called Deep Freeze Quantization (DFQ). DFQ introduces an initial scale factor for each layer and token type, frozen during PTQ and pre-learned from a small set of representative calibration samples. We will investigate various initial scale learning schemes, including least-squares regression, adaptive learning rates, and manually-defined scales based on network architectures.
CONTROLS: We will compare DFQ with different initial scale learning schemes to techniques such as data-dependent quantization and compare its impact on VGGT's accuracy after PTQ on ScanNet.
COST: 12096
PREDICTION: We expect DFQ to improve the robustness and accuracy of PTQ for VGGT in 3D reconstruction tasks, especially when dealing with special tokens. However, empirically selecting the best initial scale factor may be challenging due to the high dimensionality of the search space.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Calibration Set Size and Diversity Effects on Post-Training Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers (revision)
PROPOSAL: We will modify the previous proposal to incorporate the use of rejection sampling to enforce diversity and representativeness in the calibration set. This involves iteratively sampling scenes from the dataset and rejecting those that are similar to previously selected scenes, ensuring that the calibration set captures diverse and representative examples of the 3D reconstruction process.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of this revised calibration approach with the baseline calibration method using a fixed and diverse set of scenes, as well as with the previous calibration approach using rejection sampling.
COST: 5760
PREDICTION: We expect the revised calibration set construction method using rejection sampling to achieve better performance in terms of generalization to unseen scenes and robustness to outlier samples, especially when the selected calibration set is small. Potential failure lies in the increased computational complexity of rejection sampling and its potential to over-sample certain scenes.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Deep Freeze Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: We will extend the Deep Freeze Quantization (DFQ) approach by incorporating a meta-learning scheme to learn the initial scales for each layer and token type adaptively. This involves training a small meta-model on a set of representative tasks and using its outputs as the initial scale factors for PTQ. We will investigate the use of different meta-model architectures, such as Transformers and ResNets, and compare their performance with other initial scale learning schemes.
CONTROLS: We will compare the adaptive meta-learning DFQ approach with the fixed-scale DFQ and data-dependent quantization techniques on ScanNet and evaluate its impact on VGGT's accuracy after PTQ.
COST: 20112
PREDICTION: We expect the adaptive meta-learning DFQ approach to improve the robustness and accuracy of PTQ for VGGT in 3D reconstruction tasks by effectively capturing task-specific and dataset-dependent patterns in the activation statistics. However, the added complexity may incur higher computational costs during training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Yield Similarity-Based Calibration Set Construction for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel calibration set construction method based on cross-yield similarity among scenes reconstructed by VGGT. This approach computes similarity measures between yields produced by VGGT on pairs of scenes and selects calibration samples from diverse yield clusters. We will evaluate the performance of this approach on ScanNet and compare it with the baseline calibration set construction methods.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the cross-yield similarity-based calibration set construction with the baseline calibration set construction methods and investigate the effect of varying yield similarity thresholds on the quality of the constructed calibration set.
COST: 10944
PREDICTION: We expect the cross-yield similarity-based calibration set construction to achieve better performance in terms of generalization to unseen scenes and robustness to outlier samples, by capturing scene yield patterns that are representative of real-world scenarios. However, the choice of yield similarity threshold may be challenging due to its sensitivity to specific scene and VGGT configurations.

PROPOSAL: We propose to extend the Deep Freeze Quantization (DFQ) approach by incorporating quantization-aware training (QAT) during the fine-tuning phase of PTQ. PROPOSAL: We will derive analytical risk bounds for post-training quantization of 3D reconstruction transformers, based on the maximum likelihood estimation of the quantization ranges. CONTROLS: We will compare the analytical and empirical risk bounds with existing results for 2D vision tasks and language models, and investigate the trade-offs between calibration complexity, quantization accuracy, and model performance.

PREDICTION: We expect the analytical and empirical risk bounds to provide valuable insights into the design of efficient and accurate post-training quantization schemes for 3D reconstruction transformers, while highlighting potential challenges and limitations of current approaches.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration-Aware Weight Quantization for Billion-Scale 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose the "QuantReg" method, where we separate weight quantization into two components: a calibration step, where we calculate the quantization ranges using a small portion of the data, and a quantization step, where we apply the actual quantization to the weights. This is done by observing that some weights are redundant or less influential in the overall model performance. We use a well-established metric like F1-score and \(\ell_2\) loss to identify the importance of each weight. The calibration step uses a well-chosen augmented dataset to select the most representative weights and optimize their quantization ranges.
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT model, uniform random selection of weights as control
COST:  1440
PREDICTION: QuantReg shows significant improvements in model performance compared to uniform weight quantization while requiring up to 2x less memory and 3x less computational resources. It may fail if the chosen importance metric doesn't accurately capture the problem; if the augmented dataset for calibration doesn't cover enough cases; or if the weight redundancies are not sufficiently explored.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Smart Tokenization for Handling Heavy-Tailed Activations
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel tokenization technique, called "Adaptive Token Embedding" (ATE), to better handle the heavy-tailed activations associated with the data-independent special tokens in the 3D transformer. ATE uses a non-linear transformation to project the activations onto a lower-dimensional space, where they become more sparse and easier to quantify. We use a learned diagonal Gaussian transform to achieve this, and train it as part of the calibration process.
CONTROLS: Standard quantization of special tokens, uniform token norm clipping
COST: 1732
PREDICTION: ATE helps reduce the impact of outliers in quantization, leading to a noticeable improvement in model accuracy and stability. However, the choice of the non-linear transformation might not always be optimal for complex 3D scenes, potentially limiting the generalizability of ATE; and if the transform is too costly to compute at inference time, it could potentially offset its benefits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamic Cross-View Activation Normalization for 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: We introduce the "DCVAN" technique, which dynamically normalizes activations across different views in the 3D transformers. DCVAN uses a learned view-normalization vector to normalize each activation's scale and shift across views, mitigating the impact of heavy-tailed distributions on quantization. This normalizer is learned jointly with the quantization parameters, ensuring that both are optimized together.
CONTROLS: Standard activation clipping, no normalization
COST:  2200
PREDICTION: DCVAN reduces the destabilizing effects of large activation values, making quantization more accurate and stable. However, the cost of computing and learning the view-normalization vectors might add to the model's computational overhead, potentially limiting its scalability on real hardware.

TITLE: Iterative Quantization and Calibration for 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose an iterative approach to jointly optimize model quantization and calibration for 3D transformers. The iterative process alternates between quantization, calibration, and a brief fine-tuning step on the quantized model. This approach helps to converge to better quantization parameters and improved calibration samples, leading to more accurate results.
CONTROLS: One-shot quantization and calibration, fine-tuning on full-precision model
COST:  2418.7
PREDICTION: The iterative approach achieves state-of-the-art results by iteratively refining the quantization and calibration steps, but its higher computational cost and number of iterations might lead to overfitting and slow convergence on complex 3D scenes and large models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Sampling for 3D Transformer Calibration
PROPOSAL: We introduce an uncertainty-aware sampling method (UAS) for 3D transformer calibration, which leverages the model's uncertainty estimates to select the most informative calibration samples. We use a Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty estimator to assign confidence scores to each sample, and select the top-scoring samples for calibration. This approach helps to reduce the variance of calibration and improve quantization accuracy.
CONTROLS: Random sampling of views, no uncertainty-based selection
COST:  2610
PREDICTION: UAS shows improved quantization accuracy and robustness to outlier samples compared to random sampling. However, the computational cost of computing uncertainty estimates might be significant, especially for large models and complex scenes.

TITLE: Meta-Learning for Adaptive 3D Transformer Quantization
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach to learning an adaptive quantization scheme for 3D transformers, which can adapt to different scenes and models. The meta-learner takes in the task-specific calibration samples and explores different quantization parameters to find the most effective ones for that task. We use a few-shot learning protocol to simulate different calibration scenarios and train the meta-learner to generalize to new scenes and models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Sampling for 3D Transformer Calibration
PROPOSAL: We introduce an uncertainty-aware sampling method (UAS) for 3D transformer calibration, which leverages the model's uncertainty estimates to select the most informative calibration samples. We use a Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty estimator to assign confidence scores to each sample, and select the top-scoring samples for calibration. This approach helps to reduce the variance of calibration and improve quantization accuracy.
CONTROLS: Random sampling of views, no uncertainty-based selection
COST:  7860
PREDICTION: UAS shows improved quantization accuracy and robustness to outlier samples compared to random sampling. However, the computational cost of computing uncertainty estimates might be significant, especially for large models and complex scenes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for Adaptive 3D Transformer Quantization
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach to learning an adaptive quantization scheme for 3D transformers, which can adapt to different scenes and models. The meta-learner takes in the task-specific calibration samples and explores different quantization parameters to find the most effective ones for that task. We use a few-shot learning protocol to simulate different calibration scenarios and train the meta-learner to generalize to new scenes and models.
CONTROLS: Single-shot quantization, uniform parameter distribution

PREDICTION: Meta-learning for adaptive quantization shows promising results by adapting to different scenes and models, but its high computational cost and requirement for large-scale meta-training data might limit its applicability to resource-constrained settings.

PROPOSAL: We present a hybrid framework that combines the strengths of multiple previous approaches to achieve state-of-the-art quantization results for billion-scale 3D transformers. The framework incorporates calibration-aware weight quantization, importance-driven weight pruning, dynamic cross-view activation normalization, iterative quantization and calibration, uncertainty-aware sampling, and meta-learning for adaptive quantization. We also introduce a novel technique to integrate the strengths of different quantization methods while minimizing their weaknesses.
CONTROLS: Baseline for comparison (e.g., full-precision model)

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Exploring Activation Clustering for Efficient Quantization
PROPOSAL: We propose to use activation clustering to efficiently quantize the activations of the data-independent special tokens in the VGGT transformer. By clustering the activations of each special token into a small number of centroids, we can represent the heavy-tailed distributions of each token using a smaller set of well-behaved clusters. This approach avoids the need for bit-width explicit quantization and can reduce memory consumption. We will cluster the activations using a hierarchical clustering algorithm and evaluate the regime in which this approach is most beneficial.
CONTROLS: Quantization-aware training, standard post-training quantization
COST: 50

PREDICTION: Our approach may show significant results in scenes where the activations of special tokens are concentrated in a few heavy tails, achieving memory reductions up to 30% compared to PTQ, while still maintaining camera pose accuracy close to the full-precision model. It might fail in cases where the heavy tails are extremely sparse or where the data distribution is highly complex, leading to sub-optimal clustering.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Synthetic Dataset for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction Calibration
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the calibration challenges associated with real-world data, we propose to create a synthetic multi-view 3D reconstruction dataset. This dataset will consist of a broad range of scenarios, including indoor and outdoor environments, various object complexities, and diverse camera configurations. We will use this dataset to train a VGGT model with proper data augmentation and then use it for calibration. By doing so, we can extensively test our quantization approaches in a controlled environment.
CONTROLS: Real-world datasets (e.g., DTU, Wingspan), random search vs. grid search for hyperparameter tuning
COST: 200

PREDICTION: This synthetic dataset should enable us to robustly evaluate various calibration methods and show the effectiveness of our activation clustering approach in real-world scenarios. However, it might fail to generalize if the synthetic scenarios do not cover a wide enough range of real-world scenarios, leading to biased performance evaluations.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Joint Calibration and Quantization with Separate Bit-Widths
PROPOSAL: We propose to jointly calibrate and quantize the activations of the VGGT model by dividing the activations into separate groups, each optimized by a distinct bit-width. For example, we can use 8 bits for the camera token and 4-6 bits for the register tokens. This approach allows us to balance the information loss and the required bit-widths for each group. We will also use a multi-objective optimization algorithm to search for the optimal bit-widths across all groups.
CONTROLS: Calibration and quantization with fixed bit-widths, separate calibration and quantization with fixed bit-widths
COST: 300

PREDICTION: Joint calibration and quantization with separate bit-widths should lead to higher accuracy in camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction, especially in scenes with diverse geometry and camera configurations. It might be computation-intensive for large models with many activation groups, and calibrating the correct bit-widths for each group within a limited number of iterations might lead to performance degradation.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Enhancing Activation Clustering with Local Normalization
PROPOSAL: We revise our activation clustering approach to incorporate local normalization. Before clustering, we will normalize the activations for each activation group within a certain radius (i.e., using a sliding window) to reduce the effect of extreme values. This should improve the quality of the clusters and, therefore, the overall accuracy of the quantized model. We will use different window sizes to study the impact of normalization on various datasets.
CONTROLS: Previous version of activation clustering, calibration and quantization with fixed bit-widths
COST: 600

PREDICTION: Normalization is likely to provide significant benefits, especially when the activation distributions within each group exhibit high variance or when the input signals have non-uniform scales. However, using excessive normalization might remove valuable information for clustering, leading to performance degradation or overfitting.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Adversarial Robustness Analysis for Quantized VGGT
PROPOSAL: We aim to assess the robustness of the quantized VGGT models we proposed by evaluating their performance under adversarial attacks. We will generate adversarial examples using various methods (e.g., PGD, C&W) and evaluate their effects on the quantized models' accuracy and robustness, as well as compare these to the baseline full-precision model. This analysis will help us understand whether our quantization methods have compromised the security or reliability of the VGGT system.
CONTROLS: Original full-precision VGGT model, other methods of variable bit-width quantization
COST: 400

PREDICTION: Evaluating adversarial robustness should demonstrate whether the activation clustering, joint calibration and quantization, and local normalization methods potentially preserve the security and reliability of the VGGT system when compressed. However, the results might vary depending on the chosen adversarial attack method and the definition of robustness, potentially leading to mixed or inconclusive findings.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Calibrating the Synthetic Dataset with Noise Injection
PROPOSAL: We revise our synthetic dataset generation to artificially inject domain-specific noises or variations to account for real-world complexities. This can help reduce overfitting and improve generalizability. We will inject noise into camera parameters (e.g., camera distortion, blur), scene complexity (e.g., object obstructions, occlusions), and other relevant factors. Additionally, we will use techniques such as Mixup or CutMix to further diversify the generated data.
CONTROLS: Original synthetic dataset, cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning
COST: 800

PREDICTION: Introducing controlled noise should make the synthetic dataset more realistic and representative of real-world scenarios, thus helping our quantization approaches better generalize. However, excessive noise may push the models' accuracy beyond realistic limits, and overinjection of noise could negatively impact the models' performance.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Bit-Wise Pruning after Quantization
PROPOSAL: We propose to apply bit-wise pruning to the weights of the quantized VGGT model, aiming to optimize both the model complexity and the number of parameters while maintaining its functionality. This approach can lead to significant memory efficiency and speedup improvements without compromising performance. We will explore pruning methods, such as quantization-aware pruning and soft pruning, and study their impact on the robustness of the model.
CONTROLS: Traditional pruning methods (e.g., OLTP, LRP), other bit-width quantization methods (e.g., PACT, BNE-z)
COST: 1200

PREDICTION: By combining quantization and pruning, we expect to see significant reductions in model size and inference time, with fewer but more critical connections between neurons, thus maintaining high accuracy on camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction tasks. However, aggressive pruning might result in performance degradation, loss of critical features, or compromised robustness under various conditions.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Separate Calibration and Quantization with Input-Specific Masks
PROPOSAL: We revise our approach to jointly calibrate and quantize the VGGT model by suggesting that the camera and register tokens be treated separately. For the camera token, we will apply a mask that captures the fixed patterns of camera movements, while for the register tokens, we will apply an adaptive mask based on the input images. This way, we can optimize the bit-widths and calibration for each input case, considering the variations in scene geometry and lighting conditions.
CONTROLS: Previously proposed joint calibration and quantization approach, traditional quantization methods
COST: 1600

PREDICTION: Incorporating input-specific masks should account for the diverse conditions of real-world scenarios and potentially result in better camera pose accuracy and point map reconstruction. However, applying such masks may add computational cost, increase model size, or lead to less generalizable outcomes if not adapted to various conditions.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Efficient Weight Quantization using Weighted K-Means
PROPOSAL: We propose to use weighted K-means clustering to quantize the model's weights. This approach allows us to assign different weights to different clusters based on the importance of the corresponding connectivity patterns. By doing so, we can achieve a tradeoff between weight accuracy and model complexity. We will compare the performance of this approach to other weight quantization methods and explore the optimal number of clusters.
CONTROLS: Previous approaches to weight quantization, traditional K-means clustering
COST: 2400

PREDICTION: Weighted K-means should provide a more nuanced understanding of the model's weights and facilitate more accurate quantization, especially when combined with activation clustering and pruning. However, it may be challenging to determine the optimal number of clusters and weights, leading to potential over-fit or under-fit conditions.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Progressive Bit-Wise Pruning with Iterative Refining
PROPOSAL: We revise our bit-wise pruning approach to incorporate an iterative refinement step, where we apply a sequence of pruning strategies with progressively reduced tolerance. We will start with a coarse pruned version of the model and gradually refine it by relaxing the pruning constraints. This allows us to maintain a delicate balance between pruning extent and resulting model quality. We will also study the effects of different iteration numbers and pruning schedules.
CONTROLS: Original progressive pruning approach, revised iterative refining methods (e.g., sequence-based pruning, passing-based pruning)
COST: 3600

PREDICTION: By iteratively refining the model with progressive pruning, we should be able to achieve a more optimal tradeoff between sparsity and accuracy, resulting in higher performance in camera pose estimation and point map reconstruction tasks while reducing model size and inference time. However, excessive iteration may lead to over-refining, causing performance degradation or exhausted model training.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Robust Calibration for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction via Adaptive Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose an adaptive sampling strategy for collecting a diverse calibration set. Our approach involves generating a set of augmented input sequences using techniques such as cutout, color jittering, and random view synthesis. We then sample randomly from this augmented set to obtain a calibration set that captures a rich representation of the data distribution. Using this set, we calculate weighted quantization ranges that account for the non-uniform coverage of the original data space.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against standard random sampling and assess its impact on the quantization results.
COST: 15000 
PREDICTION: Our adaptive sampling strategy should lead to more accurate quantization ranges due to improved representation of the data distribution. However, it may suffer from overfitting if not combined with regularization techniques, such as early stopping or weight decay, which could degrade performance when few samples are available.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Special Token Handling via Channel-wise Scaling Factor Learning
PROPOSAL: Since data-independent special tokens can cause heavy-tailed activation distributions, we introduce a new module that learns channel-wise scaling factors for these tokens. This allows the model to reweight the activations and convert them back into more balanced distributions, alleviating the issues caused by extreme variance. The scaling factors are predicted by a new transformer block that processes the special tokens and the learned register tokens in parallel.
CONTROLS: We compare against a baseline where no special token handling is implemented and evaluate the impact of different scaling factor learnability regimes, such as fixed and learned scaling.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: This approach should significantly improve the robustness of the quantization by handling the heavy-tailed distributions associated with data-independent special tokens. However, it may add considerable inference cost, and its effectiveness might diminish on smaller datasets where the model has less capacity to learn from.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Multistream Quantization for Efficient 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: To address the issue of static quantization ranges across different tasks and input sequences, we propose a multistream approach where each stream is dedicated to a specific 3D reconstruction task (e.g., depth estimation, point map regression, camera pose prediction). Each stream has its own learnable quantization parameters, allowing the model to adapt to different task requirements and optimize resource utilization.
CONTROLS: We compare the multistream approach against single-stream quantization and assess its impact on Inference time, accuracy, and memory usage. We also evaluate the effect of changing the number and types of tasks handled by each stream.
COST: 26750 
PREDICTION: This approach should offer significant improvements in adaptation to diverse tasks and optimization of resource usage. However, it might introduce an additional layer of complexity, making it harder to optimize and prune the model. Its effectiveness in different regimes and domain shifts should be further examined.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: An Importance-Sampling-Based Framework for Robust Quantization Parameter Learning
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of learning representative quantization parameters under the strain of heavy tails in activation distributions, we present a new importance-sampling-based framework. This framework reweights the data to reduce the effects of extreme values, thus facilitating more accurate estimation of quantization parameters. We further extend this framework to incorporate adaptive importance sampling and adaptive quantization range learning.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the performance of our framework in the presence of different data distributions and compare it against standard quantization parameter learning methods.
COST: 35000 
PREDICTION: This framework should yield more accurate quantization parameters by adaptively focusing on informative regions of the data distribution, thereby addressing the challenges posed by data-independent special tokens. However, the choice of importance sampling strategy and reweighting schemes might have a significant impact on the overall effectiveness of this approach.

The recurrent model analyzes the temporal dependencies within the special tokens, while the weight fusion scheme aggregates the predictions from multiple scaling factor estimators. TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers via Bayesian Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: To make the quantization process more robust and reliable, we incorporate Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) to estimate the uncertainty of the model's predictions. This uncertainty-aware approach enables us to quantify the confidence in our quantization decisions and adaptively adjust the quantization parameters based on the uncertainty of the model.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the uncertainty-aware BNN-based quantization against traditional quantization methods under different scenarios of model uncertainty and confidence.
COST: 48400 
PREDICTION: By embracing the uncertainty of the model predictions, we should be able to improve the robustness and reliability of the quantization process, especially in cases where uncertainty is high. However, the incorporation of BNNs may add complexity to the quantization pipeline, which could impact the inference speed and memory requirements.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating PTQ for Billion-Scale 3D Reconstruction Transformers: Baseline Experiment
PROPOSAL: Experiment with the full-precision VGGT model on the 7-Scenes dataset, evaluating it using metrics such as pose error (via  normalized positional error), depth accuracy, and point cloud completion score.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed full-precision VGGT to pre-trained, task-specialized 3D reconstruction models such as M Wonka and S M. Liu's PointRCNN for pose estimation and depth completion, and Lingxi Xie's Deep Hairston for point cloud reconstruction.

PREDICTION: The full-precision VGGT will outperform existing task-specialized models by a significant margin, but will be memory-inefficient and unable to deploy in resource-constrained settings, indicating the need for accurate quantization methods.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: PTQ for VGGT Weight Quantization: Binary and Ternary Experiments
PROPOSAL: Perform post-training quantization of the VGGT weights using binary and ternary versions of the celebrated DeepSpeed ZeRO-Optimized quantization algorithm, and evaluate the binary and ternary models on the 7-Scenes dataset with the same metrics as in Proposal 1 (pose error, depth accuracy, point cloud completion score).
CONTROLS: Ablate the special tokens injection and focus on pure image tokens, while also investigating whether training separate neck modules can improve quantization quality.
COST: 1,500,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: While the binary and ternary models will suffer a moderate drop in performance ( < 10% in terms of pose error), they will achieve a 2-3x reduction in memory usage, paving the way for the limited application of VGGT in real-world 3D reconstruction tasks with constrained resources.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Calibration-Aware Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers: Study of Calibration Datasets and Batch Sizes
PROPOSAL: Design and train a series of calibration datasets with varying degrees of complexity and realism, spanning sizes from 128 images to 4096 images, to determine the minimum size required for reliable calibration of VGGT's special tokens and 7-scene point clouds. Experiment with various batch sizes to find the optimal trade-off between calibration efficiency and calibration accuracy.
CONTROLS: Analyze the sensitivity of the calibration process to the size and diversity of the calibration set, as well as the batch size during calibration.
COST: 2,500,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The results will show that a calibration set of 1,024 to 2,048 images is optimal, while calibration set diversity will significantly improve the robustness of the quantization ranges to outliers and unseen scenes, leading to up to 20% better average pose accuracy in unseen scenes.

CONTROLS: Compare the proposed adaptive quantization methods (QAT and online quantization) to traditional post-training quantization, and analyze their effect on VGGT performance in terms of accuracy and memory usage.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating PTQ for Billion-Scale 3D Reconstruction Transformers: Baseline Experiment
PROPOSAL: Experiment with the full-precision VGGT model on the 7-Scenes dataset, evaluating it using metrics such as pose error (via  normalized positional error), depth accuracy, and point cloud completion score.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed full-precision VGGT to pre-trained, task-specialized 3D reconstruction models such as M Wonka and S M. Liu's PointRCNN for pose estimation and depth completion, and Lingxi Xie's Deep Hairston for point cloud reconstruction.
COST: 1,000,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The full-precision VGGT will outperform existing task-specialized models by a significant margin, but will be memory-inefficient and unable to deploy in resource-constrained settings, indicating the need for accurate quantization methods.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: PTQ for VGGT Weight Quantization: Binary and Ternary Experiments
PROPOSAL: Perform post-training quantization of the VGGT weights using binary and ternary versions of the celebrated DeepSpeed ZeRO-Optimized quantization algorithm, and evaluate the binary and ternary models on the 7-Scenes dataset with the same metrics as in Proposal 1 (pose error, depth accuracy, point cloud completion score).
CONTROLS: Ablate the special tokens injection and focus on pure image tokens, while also investigating whether training separate neck modules can improve quantization quality.
COST: 4,500,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: While the binary and ternary models will suffer a moderate drop in performance ( < 10% in terms of pose error), they will achieve a 2-3x reduction in memory usage, paving the way for the limited application of VGGT in real-world 3D reconstruction tasks with constrained resources.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Calibration-Aware Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers: Study of Calibration Datasets and Batch Sizes
PROPOSAL: Design and train a series of calibration datasets with varying degrees of complexity and realism, spanning sizes from 128 images to 4096 images, to determine the minimum size required for reliable calibration of VGGT's special tokens and 7-scene point clouds. Experiment with various batch sizes to find the optimal trade-off between calibration efficiency and calibration accuracy.
CONTROLS: Analyze the sensitivity of the calibration process to the size and diversity of the calibration set, as well as the batch size during calibration.
COST: 7,500,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The results will show that a calibration set of 1,024 to 2,048 images is optimal, while calibration set diversity will significantly improve the robustness of the quantization ranges to outliers and unseen scenes, leading to up to 20% better average pose accuracy in unseen scenes.

COST: 8,200,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The results will show that QAT can achieve memory efficiency gains comparable to PTQ, while online quantization can adapt to the changing activation distributions at inference time and leading to around 10% better average pose accuracy in unseen scenes compared to baseline quantization methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring DPT with Gaussian Mixture Models for Continuous Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: This experiment modifies DPT to use a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) for the action distribution. The GMM will be trained to capture complex, multi-modal continuous action posteriors, allowing actions to be sampled natively at inference time and preserving the agent's interpretation as posterior sampling. We will compare the GMM-based DPT with the vanilla DPT on a collection of continuous-control tasks in the robot manipulation and locomotion domains, including MuJoCo and robotics tasks from the reinforcement learning benchmark repository.
CONTROLS: (1) Vanilla DPT, (2) Vanilla DPT with a fixed Gaussian distribution for the action space, (3) AD as a baseline for in-context reinforcement learning.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The GMM-based DPT is expected to outperform vanilla DPT and the fixed Gaussian distribution on tasks that have complex, multi-modal action distributions. However, it may struggle with tasks that require high-dimensional action spaces due to the curse of dimensionality in GMMs.

TITLE: In-Context Exploration for DPT in Unseen Tasks
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to investigate DPT's ability to adapt to entirely unseen tasks and parametric variations of known environments using in-context exploration. We will train DPT on a collection of tasks in the robot manipulation and locomotion domains, and then use in-context exploration to adapt to novel tasks and variations of the training tasks.

TITLE: Investigating Temporal Embeddings for DPT
PROPOSAL: This experiment incorporates temporal embeddings into the DPT architecture to improve its ability to learn policies that adapt to changes in the environment over time. However, the increased model complexity may make the DPT with temporal embeddings more prone to overfitting, especially when trained on a limited number of tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring DPT with Gaussian Mixture Models for Continuous Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: This experiment modifies DPT to use a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) for the action distribution. The GMM will be trained to capture complex, multi-modal continuous action posteriors, allowing actions to be sampled natively at inference time and preserving the agent's interpretation as posterior sampling. We will compare the GMM-based DPT with the vanilla DPT on a collection of continuous-control tasks in the robot manipulation and locomotion domains, including MuJoCo and robotics tasks from the reinforcement learning benchmark repository.
CONTROLS: (1) Vanilla DPT, (2) Vanilla DPT with a fixed Gaussian distribution for the action space, (3) AD as a baseline for in-context reinforcement learning.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The GMM-based DPT is expected to outperform vanilla DPT and the fixed Gaussian distribution on tasks that have complex, multi-modal action distributions. However, it may struggle with tasks that require high-dimensional action spaces due to the curse of dimensionality in GMMs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: In-Context Exploration for DPT in Unseen Tasks
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to investigate DPT's ability to adapt to entirely unseen tasks and parametric variations of known environments using in-context exploration. We will train DPT on a collection of tasks in the robot manipulation and locomotion domains, and then use in-context exploration to adapt to novel tasks and variations of the training tasks.
CONTROLS: (1) DPT without in-context exploration, (2) AD as a baseline for in-context reinforcement learning, (3) a random exploration baseline.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The in-context exploration-based DPT is expected to improve upon the vanilla DPT and the baseline methods on unseen tasks and parametric variations of the training tasks. However, the effectiveness of in-context exploration may decrease as the number of task variations increases due to the limited expressiveness of the DPT model's action policy.

TITLE: Investigating Temporal Embeddings for DPT
PROPOSAL: This experiment incorporates temporal embeddings into the DPT architecture to improve its ability to learn policies that adapt to changes in the environment over time. We will use a learnable temporal embedding module to encode the time dimension of the environment's state and action sequences, and then use this embedding to inform the DPT's policy outputs. We will evaluate the effectiveness of this approach on a collection of tasks in the robot manipulation and locomotion domains that involve temporal dependencies, such as the "Walker" and "HalfCheetah" tasks from the MuJoCo benchmark.
CONTROLS: (1) Vanilla DPT, (2) DPT with a fixed temporal embedding, (3) DPT with a learned temporal embedding but without the embedding informing the policy outputs.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The DPT with temporal embeddings is expected to outperform the vanilla DPT on tasks that involve temporal dependencies, as it will be better able to capture and adapt to changes in the environment over time. However, the increased model complexity may make the DPT with temporal embeddings more prone to overfitting, especially when trained on a limited number of tasks.

TITLE: Investigating Temporal Embeddings for DPT
PROPOSAL: This experiment modifies the DPT architecture to incorporate a graph neural network (GNN) embedding module to capture spatiotemporal dependencies in the environment's state and action sequences. The GNN embeds the sequence of states and actions into a graph-structured representation, which is then used to inform the DPT's policy outputs. We will evaluate the effectiveness of this approach on a collection of tasks in the robot manipulation and locomotion domains that involve spatiotemporal dependencies, such as the "Ant" task from the MuJoCo benchmark.
CONTROLS: (1) Vanilla DPT, (2) DPT with a fixed temporal embedding, (3) DPT with a learned temporal embedding but without the embedding informing the policy outputs, (4) GNN architecture without the DPT policy.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The DPT with GNN-based temporal embeddings is expected to outperform the vanilla DPT on tasks that involve spatiotemporal dependencies, as it will be better able to capture and adapt to changes in the environment over time and space. However, the increased model complexity may make the DPT with GNN-based temporal embeddings more prone to overfitting, especially when trained on a limited number of tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: DPT-based In-Context Learning with Conditional Normalizing Flows for Multi-Domain Continuous Control
PROPOSAL: We will train a DPT-based agent using a synthetic multi-domain dataset, where continuous actions are represented by conditional normalizing flows (CNFs) that model complex multi-modal posteriors. At inference time, we will sample actions natively from these CNFs. We will also explore ensemble methods, where multiple CNFs are combined to improve robustness.
CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT on the same dataset, an ablation study removing CNFs.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Expected to see strong performance across multiple domains, but potential challenges in accurately capturing posterior distributions and adapting to diverse environments, leading to failures in some domains where the CNF struggles.

CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT without exploration, and a separate evaluation of the domain-agnostic exploration policy.

PROPOSAL: We propose to apply Efficient Trajectory Refraction (ETR) to the DPT-based model to improve its ability to adapt to complex environments with diverse action and observation spaces. ETR will help the model to focus on the most informative regions of the state space, reducing the sampling complexity and improving the efficiency of the in-context learning process.

PROPOSAL: We propose a modulated DPT architecture where the model is conditioned on a learned domain-agnostic exploration policy, which is trained simultaneously with the DPT. This policy guides the model in exploring novel actions without requiring domain-specific knowledge. We will evaluate on a subset of continuous-control tasks from various domains.
CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT without exploration, and a separate evaluation of the domain-agnostic exploration policy.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved generalization across tasks and domains, but potential challenges in balancing exploration and exploitation, leading to suboptimal performance on some tasks where exploration is detrimental.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED DPT-based In-Context Learning with Conditional Normalizing Flows for Multi-Domain Continuous Control
PROPOSAL: To improve the model's ability to handle varying action and observation spaces across domains, we will also integrate a meta-learned feature extractor that adapts to the input space of each task. This feature extractor will be trained jointly with the DPT. We will also evaluate its performance on a variety of tasks with diverse action and observation spaces.
CONTROLS: Original DPT-based model without meta-learned feature extractor, and an ablation study on the contribution of the feature extractor.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Expected to see significant improvements in the model's ability to generalize across tasks with diverse input spaces, but potential challenges in meta-learning the feature extractor for complex tasks, leading to decreased performance in those cases.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: REVISED DPT-based In-Context Learning with Conditional Normalizing Flows for Multi-Domain Continuous Control
PROPOSAL: To address the potential challenges in accurately capturing posterior distributions and adapting to diverse environments, we will modify the CNFs to incorporate a learned domain-specific prior distribution, which is adapted simultaneously with the model. This will allow the model to better capture task-specific distribution shifts.
CONTROLS: Original DPT-based model with CNFs, and an ablation study on the contribution of the learned prior.
COST: 720
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved performance across multiple domains, with better adaptation to task-specific distribution shifts, but potential challenges in learning and scaling the prior distributions for complex tasks, leading to decreased performance in those cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Trajectory Refracting for DPT-based In-Context Learning in Complex Environments
PROPOSAL: We propose to apply Efficient Trajectory Refraction (ETR) to the DPT-based model to improve its ability to adapt to complex environments with diverse action and observation spaces. ETR will help the model to focus on the most informative regions of the state space, reducing the sampling complexity and improving the efficiency of the in-context learning process.
CONTROLS: DPT-based model without ETR, and an ablation study on the contribution of ETR.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Expected to see significant improvements in efficiency and sample complexity reduction, but potential challenges in learning the refracting regions and adapting to tasks with high-dimensional observation spaces, leading to decreased performance in those cases.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED Modulated DPT with Domain-Agnostic Action Exploration for Improved Generalization
PROPOSAL: We will modify the domain-agnostic exploration policy to incorporate an information-theoretic objective that encourages exploration in regions of the action space with high uncertainty, while balancing exploration and exploitation. This will enable the model to adapt more efficiently to new tasks and domains.
CONTROLS: Original Modulated DPT model without the information-theoretic objective, and an ablation study on its contribution.
COST: 1080
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved adaptation to new tasks and domains, with better exploration-exploitation trade-offs, but potential challenges in balancing the objective with the exploration policy's propensity for high variance, leading to over-exploration and decreased performance in some cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Task-Agnostic Regularization for Improving Generalization of DPT-based Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to add a task-agnostic regularization term to the DPT-based model to encourage generalization across tasks. The regularization term will be trained simultaneously with the model and will use a meta-learning objective that minimizes the difference in behavioral responses across tasks. This will enable the model to capture generic patterns and relationships across tasks that are not specific to individual tasks.
CONTROLS: DPT-based model without task-agnostic regularization, and an ablation study on its contribution.
COST: 1260
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved generalization across tasks, with better capture of generic patterns and relationships, but potential challenges in balancing regularization and the model's propensity to overfit to specific tasks, leading to decreased performance in some cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:Span-based Dynamic Pricing for In-Context Learning with DPT-based Models
PROPOSAL: We propose to incorporate a span-based dynamic pricing mechanism into the DPT-based model to optimize the use of context data in in-context learning. The mechanism will dynamically allocate context data to the model based on its predicted ability to improve its behavioral responses, thus achieving the optimal trade-off between exploration and exploitation. This will enable the model to adapt more efficiently to new tasks and domains.
CONTROLS: DPT-based model without span-based dynamic pricing, and an ablation study on its contribution.
COST: 1530
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved adaptation to new tasks and domains, with better trade-off between exploration and exploitation, but potential challenges in learning the optimal pricing strategy and dynamic allocation of context data, leading to decreased performance in some cases.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: REVISED Efficient Trajectory Refracting for DPT-based In-Context Learning in Complex Environments
PROPOSAL: We will modify the Efficient Trajectory Refracting (ETR) mechanism to incorporate a learnable projection matrix that adaptively refines the refracting regions based on the model's uncertainty and the task's dynamics. This will enable the model to adapt more efficiently to complex environments with diverse action and observation spaces.
CONTROLS: Original ETR mechanism without learnable projection matrix, and an ablation study on its contribution.
COST: 1830
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved adaptation to complex environments, with better capture of task dynamics and model uncertainty, but potential challenges in learning and scaling the projection matrix, leading to decreased performance in some cases.

TITLE: Adaptive Ensemble of DPT-based Models for Robust In-Context Learning in Uncertain Environments
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop an adaptive ensemble of multiple DPT-based models that leverages their individual strengths and compensates for their weaknesses. The ensemble will be adapted based on the uncertainty of the environment and the models' confidence in their predictions, ensuring robust performance in uncertain and complex environments.
CONTROLS: Individual DPT-based models, and ablation study on the contribution of the ensemble.
COST: 2160
PREDICTION: Expected to see improved robustness and adaptability to uncertain environments, but potential challenges in learning and scaling the ensemble, leading to decreased performance in some cases.

PROPOSAL: Implement Meta-Transformers as a backbone architecture for DPT, pretraining on a common set of continuous-control tasks. Evaluate pretraining on tasks from different categories (e.g., object manipulation, locomotion, grasping) and fine-tune on individual tasks in the test domain. Metrics: mean episode return, success rate, ratio of times the agent selects the optimal action. Baselines: DPT with vanilla transformer backbone, PPO (deep RL baseline).

PREDICTION: Meta-Transformers provide better pretraining by capturing intra- and inter-task structure, leading to higher success rates and episode returns. However, on harder test tasks, differences may decrease or the model might underfit due to the linearity of the meta-learned embedding.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Action Representation Learning with Hierarchical VAEs for Scalable DPT
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hierarchical Variational Autoencoder (hVAE) for complex action representations in DPT. Train the hVAE on preprocessed action sequences from a diverse set of continuous-control tasks, focusing on disentangled action space dimensions (e.g., goal-oriented vs. coordinative actions). Modify the action distribution in the DPT framework to utilize the learned hVAE representation at inference time. Evaluate the hVAE's ability to capture task-agnostic and task-specific knowledge, and how this representation benefits DPT on test tasks. Metrics: mean episode return, distance between learned action embeddings, KL-divergence between action prior and posterior.
CONTROLS: compare with standard importance sampling and evaluate an ablation of the hVAE by reverting to a standard Gaussian or a multivariate normal distribution.
COST: 62750
PREDICTION: Hierarchical VAE-based action representations improve DPT's ability to reason about complex, multivariate actions, leading to higher returns and success rates across diverse test environments. The approach, however, might require retraining of the hVAE on new tasks to adapt to changing action spaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: In-Context Transfer Learning with Adaptive Weight-Sharing for Efficient Learning on Unseen Tasks
PROPOSAL: Introduce an adaptive weight-sharing mechanism between tasks, leveraging the In-Context learning capabilities of DPT, to learn an optimal set of shared weights that can be transferred across tasks while adapting to task-specific differences. Implement an adaptive set of task-specific weights trained with an attention-based loss function during task-specific fine-tuning. Evaluate performance on a diverse set of unseen control tasks and compare with baseline methods that rely on task-specific training from scratch.
CONTROLS: evaluate ablations of the adaptive weight-sharing mechanism (full weight sharing, no weight sharing, different weight-sharing layers) and an experiment varying the size of the attention head over tasks files
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: Adaptive weight-sharing enables efficient learning on unseen tasks, significantly reducing the need for task-specific fine-tuning and achieving high-performance across a wide range of control tasks. However, adapting to highly divergent tasks requires finely-tuned hyperparameter tuning to prevent information poisoning.

TITLE: Robustness and Stability Analysis of In-Context RL Methods Under Distribution Shifts
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness and stability of the proposed in-context RL methods under distribution shifts, including concept drift, covariate shift, and changes in task distribution. Develop a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess the robustness of each method, including metrics such as out-of-distribution performance, robustness to task perturbations, and robustness to changes in data distribution.
CONTROLS: compare the robustness of the DPT-style in-context learners, task-agnostic reward model, and adaptive weight-sharing mechanism under different distribution shifts.
COST: 210000
PREDICTION: The proposed in-context RL methods exhibit varying degrees of robustness to distribution shifts, with the task-agnostic reward model demonstrating strong robustness to changes in task distribution. However, they also exhibit specific vulnerabilities to concept drift and changes in action space.

REVISION: Incorporate multimodal inference (MMI) to jointly predict the optimal action and an uncertainty measure, using a probabilistic graphical model (PGM) composed of a Bayesian neural network (BNN) and Gaussian Processes (GPs). TITLE: Multitask DPT with Multi-modal Action Distribution
PROPOSAL: Introduce a multitask DPT architecture, pretraining a single model on a large synthetic dataset of transitions from multiple continuous-control domains, and equipped with a conditional prior for the action distribution, parameterized by a mixture of loc-scale Gumble-softmax distributions. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hybrid Online-Offline Learning for Progressive Environment Complexity
PROPOSAL: Incorporate an online learning component into the multitask DPT architecture, allowing the model to adapt its policy through self-interaction during testing, storing the ratings from interaction into a replay buffer, and occasionally replaying the buffer samples and optimizing the model using a simple gradient-based method. This will progressively increase environment complexity, fostering adaptation and addressing potential plateauing of performance.
CONTROLS: Multitask DPT with Multi-modal Action Distribution, Online Distillation of Experts for Tabletop Pick-and-Place and Block Stacking Tasks, GradientA2C
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Incorporating online learning should improve and stabilize the model's performance across incremental environment increases, including in highly dynamic and rapidly changing tasks like autonomous driving, however, retraining and extra computational overheads might dampen results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample-Efficient Hierarchical DPT for Multi-Domain Continuous-Control
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate a hierarchical extension of the Decision Pretrained Transformer (DPT), where the coarse policy is learned on a task-agnostic objectives (e.g., policy entropy maximization) and the fine policy is conditioned on the task context and learns online to sample from the environment. The coarse policy learns a good exploration-exploitation balance independently of the task, while the fine policy adapts to the task specifics. This hierarchical approach could mitigate the challenges of scaling DPT to diverse continuous-control environments.
CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT, DPT with diagonal Gaussian action distributions, random exploration baseline
COST: 10,000
PREDICTION: Expected to significantly boost sample efficiency in adapting to new tasks, but fine-tuning the best hierarchical architecture for diverse domains may be challenging, and ensuring that both coarse and fine policies remain aligned with the reward signal remains an open issue.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Action Distribution Learning for DPT
PROPOSAL: We introduce a new action distribution learning scheme for DPT that decouples the learning of the action space structure from the decision-making process. This involves precomputing a comprehensive action embedding projection matrix using offline data, which is then used to project any task's action space into a task-agnostic latent space. This approach can handle diverse action spaces, such as those encountered in the robotics and process control domains, while allowing the DPT to leverage the resulting structure.
CONTROLS: DPT with diagonal Gaussian action distributions, precomputed projection matrix baseline, DPT with variable action space bounds
COST: 15,000
PREDICTION: This method should allow DPT to better adapt to continuous action spaces with varying structures, but tuning the quality of the precomputed action embeddings might require a significant offline computations overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bayesian Motion Forecasting for DPT
PROPOSAL: We propose using a Bayesian motion forecasting approach to predict the future state of the system or agent in multi-step lookahead tasks. This involves modeling the uncertainty in the future states using a Gaussian Process and using the DPT to predict the distribution over possible actions conditioned on the forecasted future state. This approach allows the DPT to capture potentially complex and high-dimensional uncertainty in the future state of the system.
CONTROLS: DPT with diagonal Gaussian action distributions, random action sampling baseline, vanilla DPT on single-step tasks
COST: 40,000
PREDICTION: This method should enable the DPT to better handle multi-step lookahead tasks with uncertain future states, but its efficiency and scalability for large state-spaces remains an open question.

This involves selecting a subset of promising actions to sample from the posterior distribution and deciding which new samples to include in the inference process based on an estimated quality metric, such as policy diversity or entropy.

TITLE: Multimodal DPT: Handling Uncertain Action Distributions in Continuous Control
PROPOSAL: We extend the DPT to handle multimodal action distributions, allowing it to express uncertainty in the optimal action given the context. This involves modeling the action distribution as a mixture of experts and incorporating an entropy-based penalty term to encourage exploration of alternative actions. The DPT can then leverage the mixed action distribution to generate multiple candidate actions that it can adaptively select based on context.
CONTROLS: DPT with diagonal Gaussian action distributions, vanilla DPT, random action sampling baseline

This involves modeling the uncertainty in the future states using a Gaussian Process and using the DPT to predict the distribution over possible actions conditioned on the forecasted future state. This approach allows the DPT to capture potentially complex and high-dimensional uncertainty in the future state of the system.
CONTROLS: DPT with diagonal Gaussian action distributions, random action sampling baseline, vanilla DPT on single-step tasks
COST: 120,000
PREDICTION: This method should enable the DPT to better handle multi-step lookahead tasks with uncertain future states, but its efficiency and scalability for large state-spaces remains an open question.

TITLE: Adaptive DPT Inference for Online Policy Correction
PROPOSAL: We propose an adaptive inference mechanism for the DPT that adjusts the posterior distribution over actions under the constraint of available computational resources or updating frequency. This involves selecting a subset of promising actions to sample from the posterior distribution and deciding which new samples to include in the inference process based on an estimated quality metric, such as policy diversity or entropy.
CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT, random action sampling baseline, vanilla DPT with fixed inference schedule
COST: 150,000
PREDICTION: This approach should enable the DPT to adapt its inference process in real-time to achieve better overall performance while dealing with time or computational constraints, but optimal settings for the quality metric and selection process remain uncertain.

TITLE: Multimodal DPT: Handling Uncertain Action Distributions in Continuous Control
PROPOSAL: We extend the DPT to handle multimodal action distributions, allowing it to express uncertainty in the optimal action given the context. This involves modeling the action distribution as a mixture of experts and incorporating an entropy-based penalty term to encourage exploration of alternative actions. The DPT can then leverage the mixed action distribution to generate multiple candidate actions that it can adaptively select based on context.
CONTROLS: DPT with diagonal Gaussian action distributions, vanilla DPT, random action sampling baseline
COST: 200,000
PREDICTION: This extension should enable the DPT to capture multimodal action distributions, improving its performance in tasks with uncertain or potentially multiple optimal actions, but finding the right balance between exploration and exploitation remains an open question.

TITLE: Ensembling DPTs for Robust In-Context Reinforcement Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose an ensembling approach to combine the predictions of multiple DPTs with different architectures, weight initializations, or training objectives. Each DPT is trained independently, and the ensemble combines their predictions using an entropy-based voting scheme. This approach can help reduce overfitting and improve the robustness of the in-context reinforcement learning performance.
CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT, DPT with input replacement, random action sampling baseline, average ensemble baselines
COST: 250,000
PREDICTION: Ensembling DPTs should improve the robustness and accuracy of in-context reinforcement learning, but selecting the optimal subset of models to ensemble and tuning their weightings may require significant computational resources.

TITLE: Task-Agnostic Meta-Learning for DPT Inference
PROPOSAL: We propose a task-agnostic meta-learning approach to learn a universal inference strategy that can be applied across multiple tasks and domains. This involves training a small set of task-agnostic meta-training tasks, focusing on learning task-invariant inference heuristics that can be applied to unseen tasks. This approach aims to enable the DPT to generalize its inference capabilities across diverse tasks and domains.
